title: Vice President for Finance and Operations
description:
Hartwick College
Vice President for Finance and Operations | Leadership profile

Position overview & strategic leadership context
Hartwick College, a private residential liberal arts and sciences institution in Oneonta, New York, invites applications and nominations for the position of Vice President for Finance and Operations.

Hartwick is dedicated to helping students thrive academically, personally and professionally. Known as The Life Balance College, Hartwick emphasizes four areas: academic excellence, career preparation, physical and emotional wellness, and financial clarity. Together, these support each student’s path through college and beyond.

Reporting directly to President Laurel Bongiorno, the Vice President for Finance and Operations serves as the College's chief financial officer, a member of the President's Cabinet and an Officer of the Corporation, serving as Assistant Treasurer.

The Vice President plays a central role in advancing Hartwick’s financial sustainability, working closely with the President, Board of Trustees and Cabinet to align financial resources with institutional priorities. With oversight of an endowment of approximately $40 million and an annual operating budget of approximately $50 million, the Vice President leads the College’s financial operations, including budgeting, accounting, financial reporting, investments, cash management, debt management, procurement, risk management and information technology, and oversees the Executive Director for Operations and Contracts.

This appointment comes at an important time for Hartwick. Under President Bongiorno's leadership, the College is advancing its Forward Momentum Strategic Plan, focused on three institutional priorities: enrollment and retention, philanthropy and financial sustainability. The plan guides efforts to support academic innovation and strengthen the College's long-term financial position. The Vice President for Finance and Operations will help implement the plan through financial planning, resource allocation and institutional investments.

Opportunities & priorities
1. Strategic financial leadership & institutional sustainability
  • Serve as the College's senior financial officer, advising the President, Board of Trustees and President’s Cabinet on financial strategy, institutional resources and long-term financial sustainability.
  • Lead financial planning and resource allocation in support of Hartwick's Forward Momentum Strategic Plan, working with institutional leadership to advance its priorities of enrollment and retention, philanthropy and financial sustainability.
  • Provide financial analysis and recommendations to guide institutional decision-making, resource allocation and strategic investments.
  • Collaborate with academic and enrollment leadership to evaluate the financial performance of existing and proposed academic programs, including graduate offerings and identify opportunities for sustainable revenue growth.
  • Partner with enrollment management to evaluate tuition pricing, financial aid strategies and enrollment projections, ensuring the recruitment and retention goals support the College’s long-term financial health.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen financial performance, improve operational efficiency and support responsible institutional growth.
2. Budget development, financial management & reporting
  • Lead the development and administration of the College's annual operating budget in collaboration with the President, Cabinet and campus budget managers.
  • Maintain a three-year rolling budget model and prepare financial forecasts and scenario analyses that account for enrollment, tuition revenue, operating expenses, capital needs and other factors affecting the College’s financial position.
  • Oversee financial accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, cash management and procurement to ensure accuracy, accountability and compliance with applicable standards.
  • Monitor financial performance against approved budgets, identify emerging issues and recommend appropriate adjustments.
  • Provide timely, accessible financial information to the President, Board of Trustees and campus leadership to support informed decision-making.
  • Coordinate the annual financial audit and uniform guidance audit, and oversee the preparation of required financial statements and reports.
3. Endowment, investments, debt, legal affairs & risk management
  • Provide executive oversight of the College's endowment and investment activities, working with the outsourced chief investment officer and appropriate Board committees to support responsible stewardship of institutional assets.
  • Serve as the College's primary liaison with external legal counsel, coordinating institutional legal matters and working with College leadership as appropriate.
  • Oversee the renewal and administration of institutional insurance coverage, including general and commercial liability, cybersecurity and other insurance policies.
  • Oversee institutional risk management by enforcing insurance requirements and coverage verification for all third-party vendors and contractors and developing internal processes that evaluate and manage risk.
  • Oversee debt management, financing arrangements and related financial and continuing disclosure obligations, including evaluation of refinancing opportunities and future borrowing needs.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable financial regulations, accounting standards, contractual requirements and institutional policies.
  • Support responsible management of donor-restricted and unrestricted resources in coordination with Advancement, Financial Aid and other College offices.
4. Business operations & institutional resources
  • Provide executive leadership and oversight for the College’s administrative and business operations, including finance and accounting, student accounts, payroll, and procurement. Oversee the Executive Director of Operations and Contracts.
  • Provide executive oversight of information technology, working with departmental leadership to support institutional systems, technology investments and operational needs.
  • Oversee financial aspects of major contracts, vendor relationships and institutional service agreements.
  • Promote efficient, responsive and service-oriented operations that support the effective use of technology and other institutional resources.
5. Governance, collaboration & institutional leadership
  • Serve as a member of the President's Cabinet, participating in institution-wide planning, policy development and strategic decision-making.
  • Serve as Assistant Treasurer and an officer of the corporation, and as staff liaison to the Board of Trustees' Audit and Compliance, Fiscal Resource Management, Facilities, and Investment Advisory committees and subcommittees, providing financial analysis, reports and recommendations to support Board oversight and decision-making.
  • Build strong working relationships with academic and administrative leaders to ensure that financial planning supports the College's educational mission.
  • Communicate financial information clearly to a range of audiences, including trustees, external regulators, faculty, staff and other College constituents.
  • Foster a culture of financial responsibility, transparency and shared accountability across the institution.
6. Team leadership & professional culture
  • Lead and support a responsive, service-oriented finance and business operations team, establishing clear expectations for performance, accountability and professional conduct.
  • Recruit, develop and retain qualified staff, encouraging professional growth, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  • Evaluate and improve financial processes, reporting systems and operational practices, using technology and streamlined procedures to improve efficiency, eliminate unnecessary work and strengthen service to the campus community.
  • Demonstrate integrity, sound judgment and a collaborative leadership approach in addressing complex financial matters.
  • Comply with all applicable College, federal, state, local and associational laws, rules and regulations.
  • Represent the College professionally in interactions with internal and external constituents.
  • Participate in significant campus activities, including Welcome Weekend, True Blue Weekend and Commencement Weekend.
Required & preferred qualifications
Required qualifications
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business administration or a closely related field.
  • Executive leadership experience: Significant progressive leadership experience in financial management, including responsibility for complex budgets, financial operations and organizational planning.
  • Financial expertise: Demonstrated knowledge of financial accounting, budgeting, financial analysis and reporting, long-range financial planning, cash and debt management.
  • Strategic planning: Proven ability to develop financial strategies, evaluate institutional risks and align financial resources with organizational priorities.
  • Management experience: Demonstrated success leading teams, managing complex operations and building effective relationships across an organization.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex financial information clearly to executive leadership, governing boards and nonfinancial audiences.
  • Professional judgment: A record of integrity, sound decision-making, accountability and responsible financial stewardship.
Preferred qualifications
  • Advanced education and certification: MBA or other relevant advanced degree and/or Certified Public Accountant (CPA) designation.
  • Higher education experience: Senior financial leadership experience in higher education or another complex nonprofit institutional environment.
  • Investment and debt management: Experience overseeing endowment investments, institutional debt, capital financing and long-term financial planning.
  • Operational knowledge: Familiarity with facilities management, physical plant operations, auxiliary services, procurement and institutional risk management.
  • Leadership style: Collaborative, consultative and service-oriented leadership, with the ability to build trust and foster productive relationships across the institution.
  • Strategic awareness: Understanding of the financial and operational factors affecting private higher education, including enrollment trends, tuition revenue, financial aid, expense management, philanthropy and institutional sustainability, with the ability to translate institutional strategic priorities into effective financial plans.
  • Institutional perspective: Ability to balance financial discipline with the academic mission and student-centered priorities of a small residential liberal arts college.
Salary Range: $160,000 - $185,000

How to apply
Hartwick operates as a community of learners where there is a strong sense of belonging and connection. Faculty and staff work together to support students, share in the College's successes and contribute to its future. Every position at Hartwick supports the education and development of students, and employees have opportunities to see how their work makes a difference.

Hartwick College is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace and a diverse candidate pool. The College encourages applications from members of underrepresented groups.
Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check.

Applicants will be asked to submit a cover letter, a resume or curriculum vitae and the names and contact information of five professional references, including at least one current or former supervisor. References will not be contacted without prior notification to the candidate.

About Hartwick College
Hartwick's work is grounded in its mission:
Hartwick College, an engaged community striving toward inclusion and equity while increasing diversity, integrates a liberal arts education with experiential learning to inspire curiosity, critical thinking, creativity, personal courage and an enduring passion for learning.

Through its distinctive FlightPath approach, Hartwick connects classroom learning with mentorship, career preparation and hands-on experiences. Students may choose from more than 60 majors and minors, as well as programs in pre-engineering, pre-law, pre-med and pre-health professions. Qualified students, across academic programs may pursue Hartwick's accelerated three-year bachelor's degree option.

Hartwick has also expanded its academic offerings with the introduction of its first Master of Business Administration (MBA) program, featuring six specializations in artificial intelligence, business analytics, cybersecurity, finance, healthcare administration and self-designed. Three new graduate programs in education include master's degrees in childhood education, adolescent education, and education, equity and innovation. Designed to be completed in one academic year through hybrid instruction, these programs create new opportunities for students, alumni and working professionals.

Under the leadership of Laurel Bongiorno, who became Hartwick’s 13th president in June 2026, the College is advancing its Forward Momentum Strategic Plan. The plan guides institutional decision-making and investments that support Hartwick’s educational mission and long-term financial health.

Living in the area
Hartwick's 425-acre hilltop campus combines access to nature with the convenience of downtown Oneonta, just minutes away. Eight miles of Table Rock trails provide opportunities to walk, hike and relax without leaving campus. A short drive away, the College's 100-acre Pine Lake campus offers another setting for outdoor recreation and community activities.

Surrounded by the wooded hills, valleys and waterways of Central New York, Oneonta offers scenic views and year-round access to outdoor activities. The area also has an active arts and cultural scene, with concerts, theater, exhibits and community events at venues such as the Foothills Performing Arts and Civic Center. Cooperstown, home of the National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum, is approximately 30 minutes away.
Oneonta is an affordable, family-friendly college town with a weekly farmers market, locally owned shops, independent bookstores, a movie theater and a roller-skating rink. Dining options include pizza, sushi, Indian cuisine, wings, boba, diners and cafes. Local gathering places also offer live entertainment, games and pool tables.

The city is about an hour from Binghamton and 90 minutes from Albany, with New York City approximately three and a half hours away and Boston about four hours away by car.

Money magazine named Oneonta one of the 50 best places to live in the United States in 2024, while SafeWise ranked it No. 4 among the safest cities in New York for 2025. The city was also included among New York's 10 most affordable small towns. The area offers a comfortable setting in which to build a career, participate in community life and establish a home.

title: 23595 - Business Administration - HMP Lindholme
company: His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service
description:
Working Arrangements & Further Information

The MoJ offers Hybrid Working arrangements where business need allows. This is an informal, non-contractual form of flexible working that blends working from your base location, different MoJ sites and / or from home (please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas). Some roles will not be suitable for Hybrid Working. Similarly, Hybrid Working will not suit everyone’s circumstances. Arrangements will be discussed and agreed with the successful candidate(s) and subject to regular review.

For nationally advertised roles, the successful candidate(s) will be appointed to a MoJ office location, which may include their nearest Justice Collaboration Centre or Justice Satellite Office. This will be discussed and agreed on the completion of pre-employment checks.

Some of MoJ’s terms and conditions of service are changing as part of Civil Service reform. The changes will apply to staff joining MoJ who are new to the Civil Service. Staff joining MoJ from other civil service employers will transfer onto the new MoJ terms if they are already on 'modernised' terms in their current post or onto 'unmodernised' MoJ terms if they are on 'unmodernised' terms at their current post. Details will be available if an offer is made.

Standard full time working hours are 37 hours per week excluding breaks which are unpaid. HMPPS welcomes part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns, where they meet the demands of the role and business needs. All applications for part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns will be considered in accordance with the HMPPS’ Flexible Working policy.

If you are a current NPS employee, this vacancy may be available on a Loan basis for up to 2 years. Applications are invited from suitable qualified staff.

The Loan/Secondment is subject to the approval of the selected candidate's Business Unit, which should be obtained before confirmation of appointment.

Benefits

Annual Leave

-The holiday year runs from 1 March. If you work a non standard work pattern your leave entitlement may be expressed in either hours or days as appropriate. Leave entitlement is calculated on a pro-rata basis and you will be advised of your actual entitlement on appointment. If you were appointed internally and your leave was previously calculated in days, this will continue to be the case.

Bank, Public and Privilege Holidays

-You are entitled to 9 days (66 hours 36 minutes) in recognition of bank, public and privilege holidays. These hours are added to your annual leave allowance. There is a requirement to work some public and bank holidays subject to your shift pattern and the operational needs of the establishment

Pension

-The Civil Service offers a choice of two pension schemes, giving you the flexibility to choose the pension that suits you best.

Work Life Balance

HM Prison & Probation Service (HMPPS) is keen to encourage alternative working arrangements. Work life balance provides greater opportunities for staff to work more flexibly wherever managers and establishments can accommodate requests to do so. HMPPS offers flexible working subject to completion of a satisfactory probationary period and NVQ

Season Ticket Advance

-After two months’ service, you’ll be eligible to apply for a season ticket advance to purchase a quarterly or longer-period season ticket for travel between home and your place of work

Childcare Vouchers

For any moves across the Civil Service may have implications on your ability to carry on claiming childcare vouchers

Training

HMPPS is committed to staff development and offers a range of training and development opportunities, including areas such as Equality and Diversity, Dealing with Challenging Behaviour, Suicide Prevention and Anti Bullying Programmes

-There are opportunities to access promotion programmes and HMPPS provides a variety of training appropriate to individual posts

-All staff receive security and diversity training and an individual induction programme into their new roles

Eligibility

-All candidates are subject to security and identity checks prior to taking up post

-All external candidates are subject to 6 months probation. Internal candidates are subject to probation if they have not already served a probationary period within HMPPS

-All staff are required to declare whether they are a member of a group or organisation which the HMPPS considers to be racist

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service Code sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. Should you feel that the recruitment process has breached the recruitment principles you are able to raise a formal complaint in the following order

  • To Transformative Business Services (0345 241 5358 (Monday to Friday 8am - 6pm) or e mail moj-recruitment-vetting-enquiries@resourcing.soprasteria.co.uk);
  • To Ministry of Justice Resourcing team (resourcing-management-office@justice.gov.uk);
  • To the Civil Service Commission (details available here)

As a Disability Confident employer, MoJ are committed to providing everyone with the opportunity to demonstrate their skills, talent and abilities, by making adjustments throughout all elements of the recruitment process and in the workplace. MoJ are able to offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns.

You will be able to request reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process within the application form. If you need additional help completing the application form, please contact the TBS Recruitment Enquiries Team.

For more information on applying for a role as a candidate with a disability or long-term condition, please watch our animated videos.

Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy.

A Great Place to Work for Veterans

The "Making the Civil Service a Great Place to work for veterans" initiative includes a guaranteed interview scheme to those who meet the minimum criteria to provide eligible former members of the Armed Forces with opportunities to secure rewarding jobs. Allowing veterans to continue to serve their country, and to bring highly skilled individuals with a broad range of experience into the Civil Service in an environment, which recognises and values your previous service in the Armed Forces.
For further details about the initiative and eligibility requirements visit:

Redeployment Interview Scheme

Civil Service departments are expected to explore redeployment opportunities before making an individual redundant. The MoJ is committed, as part of the Redeployment Interview Scheme, to providing opportunities to those who are 'at risk of redundancy'.

MoJ is able to offer an interview to eligible candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns. Candidates will not be eligible for the Redeployment Interview Scheme if they are applying on promotion.

Civil Service Nationality Rules

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals

title: Software Engineer, Linux Kernel (Starlink)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, LINUX KERNEL (STARLINK)

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

We design, build, and operate the largest AI supercomputers in the world, from the ground up. As a member of the Platform Core team, you will be responsible for the lowest layers of the software stack on the devices setting the pace for how fast we can push the frontier of AI. Our team’s software interfaces directly with the core hardware of the supercomputer and its network fabric.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Build and maintain the lean, high-reliability Linux-based operating system that underpins our supercomputer network fabric and Starlink laser mesh of satellites.
  • Write (or rewrite) high-performance device drivers to extract the maximum physical capability from our network and compute hardware.
  • Manage deployment, operation, and debugging of our platform in production, including:
    • Rigorous resolution and root-causing of anomalies to ensure the system is constantly improving in reliability.
    • Developing and constantly improving our tools for observability and configuration management.
  • Collaborate with our hardware teams and external partners to design the next generation of supercomputer hardware and then bring up our OS and software stack on it.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or science discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in software development in lieu of a degree (internship experience is applicable).
  • Hands-on system programming experience in C or C++.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Deep knowledge of the Linux kernel and its networking stack or experience with another production-grade kernel.
  • Proficiency with debugging tools spanning kernel, network, and userspace (e.g., ftrace, perf, Wireshark/tcpdump, eBPF, gdb, and more).
  • Experience bringing up new hardware from scratch — you have flashed bare-metal software on a microcontroller with JTAG, or bootstrapped a Linux kernel and rootfs on new hardware.
  • Demonstrated track record of developing and optimizing device/peripheral drivers ideally for high-speed interfaces, or with advanced considerations like DMA and cache coherency.
  • Understanding of major peripheral hardware interface standards (Ethernet, PCIe, I2C, SPI, etc.) — you can critically review a schematic, and debug these interfaces if needed.
  • Experience with product security, OS/system hardening, and secure boot schemes.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $125,000.00 - $165,000.00
Level 2: $145,000.00 - $200,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. Company shuttles are offered to employees for roundtrip travel from select Seattle locations to the SpaceX Redmond office Monday to Friday.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

title: Survey Technician

Control Point Associates is not your average surveying firm — we are a dynamic team committed to delivering exceptional surveying services. With over 30 years of experience in land surveying, we specialize in services like construction stakeouts, boundary surveys, and 3D laser scanning, serving industries such as construction, engineering, and land development.

Our team is expanding, and we’re looking for an experienced, highly technical Survey Technician to join us in Fort Lauderdale, FL. This role is focused on survey computations, boundary analysis, and technical plan development — not field work or entry-level CAD drafting. If you're a skilled Survey Technician who thrives in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment, we want to hear from you!
Why Control Point Associates?

title: Electrical Lineman, Medium Voltage (Starship)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

ELECTRICAL LINEMAN, MEDIUM VOLTAGE (STARSHIP)

As a Medium Voltage Electrical Lineman, you will support the installation, inspection, testing, maintenance, and repair of electrical equipment in substations and power grid facilities to ensure safe, reliable power delivery. This role focuses on basic tasks under direct supervision, working with energized equipment up to 260 volts initially, progressing to higher voltages (above 750 volts) after training. You will assist higher-classified personnel in high- and medium-voltage environments, following strict safety standards. This position combines core responsibilities from substation technician and station electrician roles, emphasizing hands-on learning and team collaboration.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Assist in installing, inspecting, maintaining, and repairing substation equipment, including breakers, transformers, switches, relays, buswork, control systems, and batteries.
  • Perform basic routine maintenance on high- and medium-voltage electrical systems, such as cleaning, lubrication, and visual inspections (e.g., checking oil levels, lights, heaters, and connections).
  • Conduct entry-level electrical testing, including using voltmeters, ohmmeters, ammeters, insulation meggers, and assisting with insulation resistance, relay, transformer, and circuit breaker tests.
  • Read and interpret basic electrical drawings, one-line diagrams, schematics, wiring diagrams, and work orders with guidance.
  • Troubleshoot simple electrical, mechanical, and control system issues under supervision.
  • Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO), grounding, clearance procedures, and safety protocols (e.g., PPE, emergency rescue techniques like steel/aerial lift rescue).
  • Assist in station switching, de-energizing equipment, placing grounds, and coordinating with operators, engineers, and utility crews during outages or Operations.
  • Help with physical tasks: digging/backfilling trenches, installing conduit/pipe/cable/wire, uncrating materials, painting structures, climbing ladders/structures (up to 50+ ft), and operating hand/power tools, portable generators, blowers, and pumps.
  • Support emergency responses to outages, faults, and call-outs for prompt service restoration.
  • Document work performed, test results, and observations accurately; maintain records and prepare basic reports.
  • Replace simple components like lamps, switches, outlets, dry cells; assist with oil sampling/handling and signal/communication systems.
  • Participate in training sessions, assist in training others, and become familiar with company safety rules, First Aid.
  • Operate company vehicles and specialized equipment; inspect and store personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Perform similar or less skilled incidental duties as assigned.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.
  • 3+ years of experience working as a licensed electrician.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Associate degree in electrical, mechanical, industrial maintenance technology.
  • Basic understanding of electrical principles (AC/DC circuits, safety standards).
  • Ability to read basic prints/drawings and use common test tools.
  • Proficiency with hand/power tools and physical tasks (lifting 50+ lbs, working at heights/confined spaces, outdoors in all weather).
  • Strong safety focus, attention to detail, and ability to work independently or in teams.
  • Knowledge of print reading for drawings, manuals, and one-lines.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Schedule varies depending on site operational needs and flexibility required regarding frequent overtime/weekend support.
  • Ability to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise.
  • Ability to rapidly change roles/responsibilities while working in a high-paced, challenging work environment.
  • Stand: Up to 6 hours per day.
  • Sit: Up to 3 hours per day.
  • Push/Pull: Up to 75lbs. (unassisted) 1-2 hours per day.
  • Overhead reach: Up to 3 hours per day.
  • Walk: Up to 3 hours per day.
  • Lift/Carry: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) 1-2 hours per day.
  • Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 3 hours per day.
  • Kneel/Crouch: Up to 3 hours per day.
  • Upper body twist: Up to 6 hours per day.
  • Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees up to 3 hours per day.
  • Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, working with high voltage, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description. Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

title: Regional Manager
description:
Company Overview

Asset Living is a third-party management firm and a proven partner in fostering thriving communities nationwide. Founded in 1986, Asset Living has decades of experience delivering exceptional value to our partners. Since the beginning, our undeniable passion has driven our organic growth from a small property management firm to one of the most trusted allies in real estate. Asset Living's growing portfolio includes a multitude of properties across the country that span the multifamily, single-family home rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, active adult, and student housing divisions.

Asset Living is a fast-growing company made up of talented individuals from diverse backgrounds that differentiate us and help us drive innovation and results for our clients and communities across the US. At Asset Living, we wholeheartedly believe 'Together We Lead, Together We Succeed. We empower each other to lead by example, collaborate, and evolve – inspired by our belief that we can continually improve as individuals and as an organization. Together, we create an environment where every voice is heard, every idea is valued, and every individual experiences opportunities to grow as our company grows. When you join Asset Living, you become part of a dynamic team that thrives on unity, unique talents, and a universal culture of winning.

Recognized as one of the nation's Best and Brightest Places to Work and ranked in the NMHC top 50 professionals, join Asset Living because of its reputation as the most trusted partner in real estate, workplace culture, and growth opportunities. Asset Living is a member of The Institute of Real Estate Management (IREM) and is recognized as an Accredited Management Organization (AMO). Together, we lead the way, and together, we achieve excellence in all that we do. Join a workplace where success is a collective journey and leadership is a shared responsibility.

Regional Manager

The Regional Manager is responsible for overseeing the entire operations of a housing community portfolio. As a Regional Manager, you will manage all phases of the operations, including personnel, leasing, maintenance, financial, administration & risk management. As an offsite leader, you will supervise all aspects of the property and staff to ensure compliance with Asset’s company policies and procedures, safety and fair housing guidelines, and liability concerns.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Personnel Management

  • Use consistent techniques & company directives to screen, hire, train, coach, and develop on-site staff
  • Ensure effectiveness of staff through ongoing training, coaching, counseling, and guidance in compliance with Asset training benchmarks
  • Deal effectively and consistently with performance problems; document adequately, communicate with direct supervisor and HR and terminate appropriately when necessary
  • Prepare request for a salary increase for Community Manager and assist with other team members if necessary; sign off on all requests from the site
  • Ensure all counseling statements, written evaluations, and salary requests are provided for review to the Regional & Senior Vice President and delivered to the Human Resource department
  • Approve all timesheets and ensure hours indicated are correct, vacation and sick time reported, and signatures available
  • Deal effectively and consistently with performance problems; document adequately, communicate with Regional & Senior Vice President and HR and terminate appropriately when necessary
  • Promote harmony and quality job performance of staff through support and effective leadership
  • Ensure staff compliance and consistency with Company policies and procedures

Financial Management

  • Achieve the highest possible net operating income through the implementation of effective cost control and revenue & leasing improvement; identify trends and recommend strategies and adjustments
  • Develop yearly operating budgets/forecasts
  • Provide monthly written evaluation of income and expense line items that are significantly over budget
  • Provide Capital improvement suggestions for the future of the site
  • Monitor all proposals and contracts for large projects at sites and check work in progress
  • Monitor & maintain the timely receipt and reconciliation of deposits, rent collections, and charges to ensure submitted on a timely basis
  • Monitor & approve the timely receipt, reconciliation, and coding of all vendor invoices
  • Ensure property closeout is completed on time and ownership financial reports are accurate

Strategic Leasing Management

  • Develop yearly marketing plan and utilize marketing strategies & systems
  • Provide marketing strategy to generate rentals or for rent increases
  • Ensure staff leasing techniques are effective in obtaining closure, follow up procedures met, signing/documentation of leases, and reporting systems are accurate and up to date
  • Deal with resident complaints, concerns, and requests to ensure resident satisfaction
  • Develop and implement resident retention programs (i.e., resident functions, special promotions, monthly newsletter, etc.)
  • Effectively show, lease, and move in prospective residents

Administrative & Maintenance Management

  • Ensure all administrative & leasing reporting is accurate, complete, and submitted on a timely basis
  • Assist with the emergency team for the property; ensures proper response and handling of all property emergencies with staff, residents, buildings, etc. within company guidelines to minimize liability
  • Manage excellent customer service and monitor service request turnaround and responsiveness of maintenance staff
  • Maintain property appearance and ensure repairs are noted and completed on a timely basis (this requires regular property inspections and tours)
  • Plan for and utilize property resources, equipment and supplies economically (i.e., obtaining bids/pricing from vendors, suppliers, and contractors, dealing with inadequate service, etc.)
  • Give direction to and monitor maintenance, construction, and rehabilitation activities to ensure quality and expediency (i.e., “walk” units to ensure make-ready and work orders are completed)

Travel

  • This position entails travel, estimated at 25-50% of work time annually. Travel may be required for property visits, conferences, training sessions, or other business-related activities.

Education & Experience

  • High School Diploma or Equivalent; Bachelor’s degree preferred or four years experience in the housing industry; or one to two years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Certified Apartment Manager (CAM) or Accredited Resident Manager (ARM) preferred
  • Ability to understand and perform all on-site software functions; basic computer skills required
  • Must have basic knowledge of Fair Housing Laws and OSHA requirements

This job description should not be considered all-inclusive. It is merely a guide of expected duties. The employee understands that the job description is neither complete nor permanent and may be modified at any time. At the request of their supervisor, an employee may be asked to perform additional duties or take on additional responsibilities without notice. This is a safety-sensitive position and may be subject to additional compliance requirements.

title: Cabulance
description:
About Northwest Ambulance

At Northwest Ambulance, we are committed to delivering compassionate, high-quality patient care to the communities we serve. Our team is built on integrity, teamwork, and a shared dedication to making a difference—one call at a time. If you're looking for a rewarding career where you can grow, lead, and serve, we'd love to hear from you.

Position Summary

We are seeking dedicated and compassionate Cabulance Driver to join our growing team. As an Cabulance driver with Northwest Ambulance, you will provide pre-hospital and interfacility care, transport patients safely, and represent our organization with professionalism and heart. Operating solo in a wheelchair-accessible van, you'll transport patients between medical facilities — handling their belongings, equipment, and paperwork — and ensure every handoff is smooth from pickup to receiving-staff report.

What You'll Do

As an Cabulance driver, your core responsibilities will include:

  • Keep the vehicle clean, stocked, and road-ready at all times
  • Arrive at facilities on schedule and assist patients into the vehicle safely
  • Transport patients along with all belongings, paperwork, and equipment
  • Provide patient care reports to receiving staff as needed
  • Collect required signatures from patients and medical staff
  • Follow all NWA policies, protocols, and safety standards

Requirements

Required:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Age 23 or older with at least 2 years of driving experience
  • Valid Driver's License - must have maintained for 2 years or longer.
  • Clean driving record - limit of 2 citations in past 36 months; DUI and other serious offenses may disqualify candidacy.
  • Able to pass background check and drug screening
  • Able to obtain CPR/First Aid certification (NWA reimburses the cost)
  • Strong communication, organization, and time-management skills
  • Ability to work extended shifts, including nights, weekends, and holiday
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, occasionally high-stress environment

Preferred Skills & Abilities

  • Outstanding interpersonal and customer service skills.
  • Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Superb time management capabilities.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift, carry, and move up to 75 lbs and perform repeated bending, kneeling, and lifting.
  • Ability to work in varied weather conditions and high-stress environments.

Benefits

What you can expect from us:

We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision insurance to ensure the well-being and health of our employees.

Regular, non-exempt field employees who are scheduled to work on designated holidays are paid a premium holiday rate of 1.5 times their regular rate for all hours worked on the holiday.

Our commitment to your financial future is reflected in our generous 401k program. We provide employer matching up to 5% of your salary, empowering you to save for long-term goals.

We understand the importance of work-life balance, which is why we provide paid time off at the rate of 2.3 hours per 40 hours worked to help you recharge, spend time with loved ones, and pursue personal interests.

To maintain a professional and consistent appearance across our team, uniforms are provided to all employees, ensuring you always look your best while representing our company.

Wages:

Wages $22.00 per hours.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Northwest Ambulance is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Reasonable accommodations are available upon request for candidates with disabilities participating in the application or interview process.

This is a safety-sensitive position. Employees in this role are responsible for performing duties that directly impact of patients, coworkers, and the public.

title: Career Services & Employer Partnerships Specialist
description:
Career Team is a leading workforce development organization on a mission to transform lives. We blend cutting-edge technology with compassionate, high-touch services to drive real, measurable outcomes in the lives of job seekers across the country. At Career Team, we’re solving today’s unemployment challenges with smart software, world-class trainers, dedicated case managers, dynamic job developers, and innovative partners. If you're passionate about making a difference and believe in the power of technology to transform lives, you’ll feel right at home here.

Employment Type: Part-Time (On-Call / Per Diem, up to 10 hours/week)

Reports To: Coaching Program Manager

Pay Rate: $30.00 / hour

Location: Remote (Virtual)

Position Summary

A core priority of this role goes beyond standard job readiness - it is about actively generating real employment opportunities, contacts, and interviews for graduates of a health & sciences university.

As the Career Services & Employer Partnerships Specialist, you will serve as the critical bridge between ambitious, qualified health & sciences graduates and hiring organizations seeking talent. Rather than taking a passive advisory approach, you will operate as an active talent matchmaker: hunting for open roles, pitching qualified candidates directly to hiring managers, and building sustainable employer partnerships.

In addition to driving employer outreach, you will execute multi-channel communication campaigns to engage recent graduates, deliver high-impact 1:1 virtual career coaching, and maintain active pipelines to accelerate graduate placement.

Key Responsibilities

1. Employer Outreach & Placement (Lead Generation & Matchmaking)

  • Opportunity Sourcing: Proactively identify and connect with hiring managers, recruiters, and companies to discover open positions, internships, and talent needs aligned with our alumni pool.

  • Talent Pitching: Act as a recruiter and advocate by directly matching and pitching qualified alumni candidates to hiring managers to secure interviews.

  • Industry Insights: Stay current on health and sciences hiring trends to provide actionable market intelligence to job seekers.

2. Alumni Engagement & Multi-Channel Outreach

  • Proactive Campaign Execution: Conduct high-energy, multi-channel outreach campaigns via email, phone, and text message to drive graduate participation in Career Services.

  • Pipeline Management: Track and maintain an active pipeline of job-seeking alumni, re-engaging them consistently to understand their evolving career goals and employment status.

  • Metric Tracking: Document all touchpoints, outreach metrics, and placement milestones in the CRM.

3. 1:1 Virtual Career Coaching

  • Targeted Coaching: Deliver impactful 30-minute 1:1 virtual coaching sessions for alumni of a specialized health & sciences university.

  • Core Topics: Guide alumni across key professional development topics, including LinkedIn optimization, resume writing, targeted networking, interview strategy, personal branding/digital visibility, navigating imposter syndrome, and entrepreneurship.

Qualifications & Requirements

Minimum Requirements:

  • Experience: 2+ years of direct experience in university employer relations, higher education career services, workforce development, or technical/healthcare recruitment.

  • Coaching Credentials: Active pursuit or completion of a recognized career coaching certification (e.g., ICF, PARWCC, Lumia, The Academies, Coach U, or equivalent).

  • Tech Stack: Hands-on proficiency with Handshake, HubSpot (or comparable CRM systems), and Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Drive, Meet).

  • Communication & Sales Mindset: Exceptional written, verbal, and phone/text communication skills with a comfortable, high-energy approach to cold outreach and candidate representation.

What Success Looks Like in This Role

  • High Engagement Rates: Successfully converting cold alumni outreach into active, ongoing 1:1 coaching relationships.

  • High Value Employer Engagement: Building relationships with high-value employers, primarily large healthcare systems and national corporations.

  • Coaching Excellence: Consistently delivering actionable, high-value career strategy plans that move alumni forward in their job search.

  • Data Integrity: Maintaining real-time accuracy in HubSpot, ensuring seamless record-keeping for engagement histories and placement pipelines.

About Career Team:
Founded in 1996, Career Team, LLC is a private workforce development organization.

Career Team’s outstanding record of accelerating the human condition has resulted in numerous honors:

  • Named by Inc. Magazine as one of America's 500 fastest growing privately held companies
  • Recipient of the US Chamber of Commerce Blue Chip Enterprise Award for innovation
  • Featured by 60 Minutes, CNN, Money Magazine, Inc. Magazine and the British Broadcasting Network as an innovative, government funded solutions program
  • Invited to the White House after being cited by the National Welfare-to-Work Partnership and National Alliance of Business as a top 10 US training provider

As a socially conscious organization, Career Team has found a healthy balance between for-profit innovation and community enrichment. Looking ahead, the organization will continue to close the nation’s opportunity divide with additional government-funded workforce sites; while also building staff capacity of workforce funding sources and industry providers. See www.careerteam.com for more information.

Career Team is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.

Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the application status of applicants or continued employment of current employees who apply for the position.

title: Education Training Specialist
description:
About the role

Comply is looking for a Training Specialist to help thousands of Comply customers turn product knowledge into confident, daily use. Comply is the champion for compliance professionals, serving more than 7,000 clients globally by merging technology, consulting, and education. This role sits on our Customer Success team, at the front line of customer adoption. You’ll spend most of your time in 1:1 training sessions tailored to each customer’s role, goals, and experience, and you’ll also lead webinars, workshops, and office hours that reach many customers at once. You’ll own the training experience end to end, from scheduling to follow-up, and use customer feedback and data to keep making it better. It’s a role built for someone early in their career who loves teaching and wants hands-on experience with customers at scale, with real potential for advancement as you grow.

You’ll love this role if you love teaching and can explain complex topics clearly to whoever is in front of you- and you’re patient, curious, organized, and energized by learning new software and new subject matter.

What you’ll do

  • Deliver 1:1 training sessions tailored to each customer’s role, goals, and level of experience.
  • Lead webinars, workshops, and office hours that help customers adopt Comply products and get value from them.
  • Build deep knowledge of Comply products and how they map to client workflows and regulatory needs.
  • Customize Customer Education content (decks, demos, guides) for specific audiences, and recommend improvements based on what you see in sessions.
  • Partner with the Customer Education leader to keep training resources accurate, current, and professional.
  • Own your training calendar end to end: scheduling, preparation, reminders, and follow-up so customers leave with clear next steps.
  • Track attendance, completion, and customer feedback, and use the results to refine session formats and topics.
  • Flag risks and opportunities you hear in sessions (low adoption, frustration, expansion interest) to CSMs and account partners, and relay recurring questions and product gaps to Support and Product.
  • Log training activity and outcomes accurately in Gainsight and other internal systems, and contribute to team projects that improve how we train our largest customer base.

What success looks like in your first 90 days

  • You’ve ramped on Comply’s products and the compliance challenges our clients face, and you’re running 1:1 sessions on your own.
  • You’ve led your first webinars, workshops, or office hours and built a reliable scheduling-to-follow-up rhythm.
  • You’re tracking attendance, completion, and feedback, and using it to improve session formats and topics.

What you’ll bring

Must-have

  • 0–2 years of experience in training, customer support, customer success, teaching, or a similar customer-facing role.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication, and comfort presenting to both small and large groups.
  • The ability to explain complex topics simply to audiences with different levels of knowledge.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail across many scheduled sessions.
  • Proficiency with Teams, the Microsoft Suite, and webinar platforms, plus comfort learning new software (spreadsheets, CRM, email marketing, support, automation, and presentation tools).

Nice-to-have

  • Interest in or familiarity with financial services or compliance.
  • Familiarity with Gainsight or a similar customer success platform.

title: Propulsion Aerothermal Analyst
description:
About the role

We are looking for a Propulsion Aerothermal Analyst who is equally proficient in performing first order calculations as they are in running CFD or developing their own analysis code. You will work across design, analysis, development, operation, and reuse scenarios in a fast-moving development environment. This is a highly technical role for someone who wants to be close to details, make consequential design decisions, and help establish the propulsion fluids systems of an orbital launch vehicle program from the ground up.

What you'll do

  • Aerothermal design of propulsion components including injectors, thrust chambers, nozzles, valves, and other fluid system parts
  • Analyze regenerative, film, and radiation cooling schemes and size cooling channels to keep wall temperatures within material limits
  • Analyze fluid transients, water hammer, priming, two-phase flow, cavitation, flow-induced loads, and feed system coupling across engine and stage fluid systems
  • Perform thermal-fluid analysis of cryogenic propellant systems, including tank thermal management, chill-down, boil-off, thermal conditioning, and insulation performance
  • Develop and validate pressurization system models (autogenous, helium, or self-pressurizing) to size pressurant requirements and predict ullage behaviour
  • Build, run, and maintain steady-state and transient thermal and fluid models using tools such as Thermal Desktop/SINDA, Fluent, CFX, EcosimPro, ESPSS, Flownex, or in-house Python/MATLAB codes
  • Conduct trade studies and sensitivity analyses on system architecture, cooling, geometry, and operating points to drive design decisions
  • Support cold flow, hot fire, stage test, and flight campaigns with pre-test predictions and post-test data reconciliation
  • Identify thermal and fluid risks and failure modes, support anomaly investigations and root-cause analysis, and recommend design or operational mitigations

Qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years of experience with one or more of the following:
  • Aerothermal analysis of aerospace propulsion components
  • Creating and running 1-D flow networks for component sizing
  • Performing 3-D CFD analysis on propulsion components
  • Combustion analysis including liquid injection modelling
  • Aerothermal analysis of cryogenic propellant systems
  • Inclination toward a fast-paced, resource-constrained environment with rapid hardware development using iterative design-build-test cycles that are central to the engineering culture
  • Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related field

Preferred

  • Conjugate heat transfer analysis using Fluent or similar CFD tools on rocket engine components
  • Aerothermal design of liquid bipropellant rocket engines
  • Experience with methane systems, including methane delivery systems
  • Exposure to complex fluid systems as well as understanding the behaviour of the mechanisms in those systems
  • Turbomachinery fluid analysis proficiency
  • Structural analysis proficiency
  • Functional proficiency in CAD (NX) and Python
  • Advanced degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related field

JOB TITLE: Case Manager
LOCATION: Gateway Medical Sobering- Albuquerque, New Mexico

Who are we?
Horizon Services, Inc. (HSI) is a nonprofit established in 1974 that offers addiction treatment with the goal of reducing substance use and mental health related challenges for people from all walks of life, including those from some of the most disenfranchised and marginalized communities. We practice our values of Integrity, Respect, Professionalism, and Compassion to provide youth prevention, youth and adult outpatient, sobering programs, withdrawal management, and co-occurring capable residential programs to support the well-being of women, men, youth, LGBTQIA+, and BIPOC clients to live healthy, fulfilling and constructive lives. HSI is an inclusive workplace and a learning community where our collective experiences
enrich each other’s growth.

The Case Manager at Gateway Medical Sobering Center is responsible for providing comprehensive care coordination and discharge services for individuals experiencing acute intoxication from alcohol, opioids, methamphetamines, or other substances. Clients often present with co-occurring behavioral health conditions and require short-term monitoring before transitioning to the appropriate level of care. The Case Manager ensures timely referrals, appointment scheduling, transportation coordination, and linkage to services such as detox, residential treatment, outpatient care, housing resources, and medication-assisted treatment (MAT). This role involves close collaboration with the Registered Nurse Program Manager, NP, PA, LVNs, EMTs, and Recovery Specialists to ensure that client needs are met within the 23-hour stabilization period, using a trauma-informed and harm-reduction approach that prioritizes dignity, safety, and continuity of care.


How can you make a difference in people’s lives?
In this role, you’ll make a difference in the lives of people with substance abuse challenges, and often with co-occurring conditions. You’ll use and grow your skills in compassionate care, crisis intervention and de-escalation, in a supportive and inclusive work environment. description:

Title: Senior Technical Program Manager-NPI

Duration: Direct Hire

Location: Austin, Texas – Onsite, with required travel 25% to the Florida.

Benefits: Excellent benefits available, including unlimited PTO, 401(k) match, a bonus percentage tied to role, fully reimbursed travel and expenses, unlimited e-learning through Coursera, and relocation assistance.


Role:

Our client, a spatial computing company building the optics and manufacturing systems behind advanced augmented reality devices, is looking for a results-driven Senior Technical Program Manager. You'll drive New Product Introduction (NPI) and process-development programs, taking new waveguide processes from early R&D through prototyping until they are qualified, scalable and ready for mass production. The client produces surface-relief waveguides in-house on custom equipment, through many nanofabrication steps.
  • Drive execution: move process-development programs from focused R&D and pathfinding, through rapid prototyping, to a scalable mass production roadmap, driving schedule, scope, and deliverables to closure
  • Work closely with process, integration, and equipment engineers to translate complex technical concepts and experimental results into clear project scopes, roadmaps, and work breakdown structures
  • Keep requirements, risk analysis, validation protocols and reports, and the transfer-to-manufacturing package on schedule as the process matures toward qualification for high-volume manufacturing
  • Facilitate communication and strategic alignment between R&D, Process Engineering, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and High-Volume Manufacturing operations
  • Proactively identify technical risks, experimental dead-ends, and readiness gaps, and develop mitigation plans to keep the qualification timeline on track
  • Chair phase-gate reviews, ensuring the right technical authorities are in the room, decisions are made on time, and actions are captured and tracked to closure
  • Maintain clear project tracking, dynamic dashboards, and executive reporting for portfolio health, scope changes, and budget allocation
  • Stand up metrics and program mechanics that show how fast process development is moving and whether a process is ready to advance based on clear readiness criteria

Qualifications:
  • 5+ years of technical program or project management experience, including process-development or NPI programs in a semiconductor, MEMS, or comparable nanofabrication environment
  • Experience driving delivery from development through qualification and transfer to manufacturing
  • Ownership of phase gates, validation protocols, and the transfer-to-manufacturing package
  • Experience shaping line design for new or future lines, including automation, specs, and data systems
  • Technical breadth to engage with and challenge process, integration, equipment, and optical engineers, translating across disciplines
  • Fluency with DOE, SPC, and yield data as the basis for judging when a process is ready, and holding the team to that bar
  • Exceptional ability to synthesize complex, highly technical engineering updates into structured, actionable insights for executive leadership and internal operational teams
  • AI-forward execution: uses modern AI tools to move faster, such as automating status synthesis and surfacing schedule and supply risks earlier
  • Willing to spend frequent time on the manufacturing floor and in cleanroom environments to observe equipment, combined with a standard office environment
  • Able to wear occasional PPE (safety glasses, steel-toed shoes, or cleanroom smocks) during equipment verification and documentation

Preferred Qualifications:
  • Process experience with diffractive or surface-relief waveguides, semiconductor, advanced lithography, or other AR/MR display optics
  • A feel for how process variation propagates into optical or display performance
  • Hardware systems engineering background with TPM experience taking products from concept to production
  • Experience across the consumer electronics product lifecycle (semiconductor, electrical, optical, to fab/launch)

Education: Masters or Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or equivalent is desired.

Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Range is $140,000 to $160,000 USD annual base salary.

title: Project Manager
description:
Job Summary

The Project Manager manages key customer projects in a manufacturing environment, from order release through shipment, ensuring they are completed on time, within budget and within scope. The Project Manager oversees all aspects of each project, including material availability, production scheduling, capacity and delivery, while setting deadlines, assigning responsibilities and reporting progress, milestones and risks to upper management. The Project Manager works directly with customers to ensure deliverables meet the applicable scope, specifications and budget. They also coordinate with Sales, Engineering, Purchasing, Production, Quality and Logistics to ensure all aspects of each project are compatible.


Job Duties & Responsibilities

  • Coordinate internal resources (production, engineering, purchasing, quality, logistics) and third parties/vendors (suppliers, subcontractors, carriers) for the flawless execution of projects and establish and maintain strong vendor relationships.
  • Ensure that all projects are delivered on time, within scope and within budget, including shipment by customer commit dates.
  • Assist in the definition of project scope and objectives, involving all relevant stakeholders and ensuring technical feasibility and manufacturability.
  • Ensure resource availability and allocation, including materials, labor, equipment and production capacity.
  • Develop a detailed project plan, including production schedule and key milestones, to monitor and track progress, and share it with customers and other staff members.
  • Manage changes to the project scope, project schedule and project costs, including customer change requests and engineering changes, using appropriate verification techniques.
  • Measure and track project performance using appropriate tools and techniques (e.g., on-time delivery, schedule adherence, cost variance and quality metrics) to analyze the successful completion of short and long-term goals.
  • Report and escalate to management as needed, including material shortages, capacity constraints and quality issues.
  • Manage the relationship with the customer and all stakeholders.
  • Perform risk management to minimize project risks, including supply chain, lead-time, capacity and quality risks.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive project documentation, including order records, specifications, drawings, certifications and customer-required quality documentation, and develop spreadsheets, diagrams and process maps to document needs.
  • Meet with customers to take detailed ordering briefs and clarify specific requirements of each project, such as specifications, materials, tolerances, testing, certifications and delivery requirements.
  • Monitor project costs, including materials, labor and margin, and adjust project constraints based on financial analysis to meet budgetary objectives.
  • Use and continually develop leadership skills.
  • Attend conferences and safety and quality training as required to maintain proficiency.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.
Skills
  • Budget Development and Cost Tracking (materials, labor and margin)
  • Project Management and Scheduling, including milestone tracking and change control
  • Process Improvement (lean, continuous improvement and root cause analysis)
  • Production and Capacity Planning
  • Supplier and Vendor Management
  • Risk Management and Problem Solving
  • Leadership and cross-functional collaboration with production, engineering, quality and logistics teams
  • Strong organizational skills, including attention to detail, multitasking and prioritization in a fast-paced environment
  • Excellent customer-facing, internal, written and verbal communication skills
Education
  • Required: Bachelor's degree in project management, business, engineering, supply chain or related field.
Work Experience
  • Required: 2 - 4 years of work experience in project management in a manufacturing or related field.
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to lift, bend, stoop and climb, and to walk and stand for extended periods on the production floor.
  • Capable of lifting up to 30 lb. on a regular basis.
  • Visual acuity required while paying attention to details.

title: Career Advisor

At Career Team, we’re solving today’s unemployment challenges with smart software, world-class trainers, dedicated case managers, dynamic job developers, and innovative partners. title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Automation
description:
About us

Coalition is the world's first Active Insurance provider designed to help prevent digital risk before it strikes. Founded in 2017, Coalition combines comprehensive insurance coverage and innovative cybersecurity tools to help businesses manage and mitigate potential cyberattacks.

Opportunities to make an impact with bold thinking are real—and happening daily at Coalition.

About the role

Coalition is building an AI Automation team to eliminate manual work and improve how teams across the company operate. As a Senior Software Engineer, AI Automation, you will lead the design and delivery of reliable, production-grade AI agents and workflows that solve meaningful business problems.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for an AI-native engineer who can move from ambiguous business problems to durable technical solutions. You will work closely with internal operators, product and data partners, and engineering teams to understand complex processes, develop reusable agent capabilities, and establish the technical patterns that allow AI automation to scale safely across Coalition.

You will balance rapid experimentation with strong engineering judgment. You will define system architecture, establish evaluation and reliability practices, and ensure that production agents operate with the appropriate controls for permissions, auditability, human review, and rollback.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical design and delivery of AI agents, reusable skills, and automation workflows used by Coalition’s internal teams.
  • Translate complex, ambiguous business processes, judgment calls, and edge cases into reliable, maintainable software.
  • Design and evolve integrations between agents and systems of record using MCP and comparable tool-integration frameworks.
  • Define architecture, interfaces, data contracts, and operational standards for production AI systems.
  • Establish evaluation strategies, quality baselines, and release criteria; use results to make sound deployment and iteration decisions.
  • Build systems with robust controls for permissions, observability, auditability, human-in-the-loop review, failure containment, and rollback.
  • Partner with data engineering and business stakeholders to ensure automations use trustworthy data and have sustainable ownership.
  • Drive technical decisions across multiple workflows, identify reusable patterns, and raise the engineering bar for the team.
  • Mentor engineers and technical partners through design reviews, implementation guidance, and practical AI engineering standards.
  • Document systems, decisions, and operating practices so that teams can safely maintain and extend what you build.

Skills and Qualifications

  • 7+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, including substantial recent experience building and shipping LLM-backed applications used by real users.
  • Demonstrated experience taking AI agents or multi-step automation workflows from prototype through reliable production operation.
  • Strong Python engineering skills and practical SQL expertise, including the ability to work directly with production data models.
  • Deep experience with prompting, tool use, agentic loops, structured outputs, multi-step workflows, error handling, and production deployment.
  • Experience designing and operating systems that integrate with business-critical systems of record.
  • Strong judgment around evaluation methodology, reliability, safety controls, and the tradeoffs required to deploy AI systems responsibly.
  • Solid production engineering fundamentals across Git, CI/CD, containers, deployment, monitoring, testing, permissions, and rollback.
  • Ability to lead technical work in ambiguous environments, influence stakeholders, and turn incomplete requirements into practical, high-quality solutions.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work directly with both technical and non-technical partners.

Bonus Points

  • Experience building or maintaining MCP servers, agent platforms, or reusable tool/skill frameworks.
  • Experience designing evaluation harnesses, test datasets, and monitoring for LLM-backed systems.
  • Background in internal tools, solutions engineering, professional services, startup environments, or founding teams.
  • Familiarity with systems such as Linear, Jira, Zendesk, Salesforce, or Snowflake.
  • Experience in insurance, fintech, cybersecurity, or another regulated environment where correctness, traceability, and controls have meaningful business impact.
  • Experience mentoring engineers or acting as a technical lead for complex cross-functional initiatives.

Compensation

As a remote-first organization, our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several Canadian geographic markets.

In Alberta, British Columbia & Ontario the base salary for this position ranges from $149,600/year up to $199,600/year.

For all other locations, the base salary for this position ranges from $134,600/year up to $184,600/year.

Consistent with applicable laws, an employee's pay within this range is based on a number of factors, which include but are not limited to relevant education, skills, job-related knowledge, qualifications, work experience, credentials, and/or geographic location. Your Recruiter can share more on the specific target salary range for your location during the interview process. Coalition, Inc. reserves the right to modify this range as needed.

Vacancy Status: This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Application Updates: Consistent with our commitment to transparency, if you are interviewed for this role, we will provide a status update on your application within 45 days of your final interview.

Perks

  • 100% medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Flexible PTO
  • Annual home office stipend and WeWork access
  • Mental & physical health wellness programs like Headspace, Lumino, and more!
  • Competitive compensation and opportunity for advancement

Why Coalition?

Work at Coalition is centered on the joint mission to Protect the Unprotected. We have built a remote-first, highly inclusive culture that welcomes people from diverse backgrounds. We trust each other to take responsibility, share ownership of outcomes, and put in the work together to protect businesses from digital risk. Coalition’s exceptional growth stems from its ability to address real-world problems for organizations of all sizes while remaining true to our founding values of character, humility, responsibility, purpose, authenticity, and inclusion.

We’re always looking for collaborative, inquisitive individuals to join #OurCoalition.

title: Beauty Associate - East Village (Mandarin Required)
description:
Position Overview

Store Staff are frontline store employees primarily responsible for merchandising, replenishment and product organization, price labels, area cleanliness, customer service, receiving support, stockroom organization, Tester / sample / display-material management, work records, and issue reporting within their assigned area.


Under the direction of the Team Leader, Assistant Store Manager, and Store Manager, Store Staff complete daily tasks according to Company standards to ensure merchandise is neatly displayed, pricing is accurate, replenishment is timely, the area is clean, service is friendly, and issues are promptly reported.


Job Responsibilities

  1. Conduct Standards & Work Discipline
    1. Maintain a neat and professional appearance; wear the required uniform, name badge, and work tools.
    2. Remain focused on job responsibilities during working hours. Do not use a mobile phone on the sales floor, gather for non-work conversations, leave the assigned post without authorization, or otherwise negatively affect the customer experience.
    3. Clock in/out, complete shift handoffs, and complete the Daily Work Process Form as required.
  3. Customer Service & Basic Assistance
    1. Proactively greet customers with a smile and provide friendly service.
    2. When customers ask about products, guide them to the appropriate shelf and provide a basic introduction. If an item is unavailable, explain politely and notify the Team Lead.
    3. Promptly escalate complaints, returns/exchanges, negative feedback, or issues that cannot be resolved.
  5. Merchandising, Replenishment & Product Put-Away
    1. Complete product shelving, front-facing, categorized merchandising, display organization, and shelf maintenance within the assigned area.
    2. Replenish and organize products as required, keeping shelves full and orderly, price labels correctly matched, and aisles clear.
    3. Return unwanted customer merchandise to the appropriate category/location or transfer it to the responsible area; do not leave merchandise piled or unattended.
  7. Expiration, Shrink & Price Labels
    1. Check for near-expiration, expired, damaged, swollen, spoiled, improperly packaged, or otherwise unsellable products.
    2. Maintain price labels, promotional labels, and POP materials; promptly report pricing discrepancies or label errors.
    3. Assist with shrink records, receiving exception records, and corrective-action feedback.
  9. Area Cleanliness & Receiving Support
    1. Maintain basic cleanliness of floors, shelves, price strips, shelf guards, promotional displays, display areas, and equipment within the assigned area.
    2. Assist with receiving, moving, sorting, shelving, stockroom organization, locating products, inventory counts, and returning materials to their proper locations.
    3. Promptly report equipment, stockroom, merchandise, or safety exceptions to the Team Leader or Store Manager.
  11. Tester / Sample / Material Management
    1. Maintain Testers, samples, trial-size products, display props, promotional gifts, and related materials as required.
    2. Promptly report missing, damaged, contaminated, expired, poorly labeled, or improperly displayed items.
    3. Do not remove, give away, sell, open, exchange, or improperly dispose of Company property without authorization.


Qualifications

  • Education: High school diploma / vocational secondary school or above.
  • Professional Experience: Experience in retail, supermarkets, convenience stores, beauty, collectible/toy retail, lifestyle retail, or service industries is preferred; candidates without experience may be trained.
  • Knowledge & Skills: Familiar with or willing to learn product merchandising, replenishment and recovery, price labels, expiration management, customer service, cleanliness, receiving organization, and basic work records.
