title: Senior Product Manager, Reporting Experiences
description:
The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.

Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.

The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.

Who We're Looking For

Reporting and data analytics represent one of the most significant areas of investment at The Trade Desk right now. After building one of the most powerful programmatic platforms in the world, we are making a comprehensive, ground-up commitment to transform how our customers interact with their data — redesigning reporting experiences across the full stack, with a mandate to build something world-class. The person who joins at this moment will help define what that looks like.

The scale of the data problem is also exceptional. The Trade Desk operates at a level matched by only a handful of companies globally — processing trillions of events, across billions of ad impressions, in real time, across every channel and market. The technical and product complexity that creates is genuinely hard, and genuinely interesting. Outside of a small number of major technology companies, few environments offer this combination of data scale, business impact, and the greenfield mandate to reimagine what's possible.

We’re looking for a product manager who loves building: someone who gets close to users, becomes absorbed in their problems, and works side by side with engineering and design to create products people depend on. You bring a craftsperson’s care to the entire experience, from the clarity of an interaction to the accuracy of the data behind it. You’ll drive major initiatives that advance our reporting experiences, with the independence to shape solutions and the accountability to see them through. You measure success by the value customers realize, and when something falls short, you investigate, learn, and keep improving it.

What You’ll Do

As a Senior Product Manager, you’ll help build the next generation of reporting experiences at The Trade Desk, turning complex advertising data into clear insights and useful actions for our customers. This is an individual contributor role with meaningful scope: you’ll drive major product investments from the first customer conversation through launch and continued improvement. Working closely with engineering, design, and the broader Reporting team, you’ll combine product vision with hands-on execution to build a world-class reporting and data suite.

  • Lead reporting initiatives from vision to customer impact. Drive investments that shape how customers explore, understand, and act on their advertising data. You’ll have the autonomy to define the approach, set priorities, and develop the roadmap—and accountability for the results. Write compelling product vision and requirements documents that connect customer and market problems to our broader reporting strategy and give teams a clear direction.
  • Get close to users and their problems. Meet regularly with advertisers, agencies, and customer-facing teams. Understand how customers monitor performance, investigate issues, share findings, and decide what to do next. Use those insights to uncover opportunities and challenge assumptions about what we should build.
  • Build with engineering and design. Work side by side with your partners to explore solutions, test ideas, and turn complex workflows into intuitive experiences. Stay engaged in the details, making thoughtful tradeoffs across usability, technical complexity, and customer value.
  • Treat data as part of the product. Make accuracy, consistency, freshness, and performance foundational requirements. Partner with engineering to ensure customers can understand the numbers they see, trust the results, and get answers when they need them.
  • Prioritize and deliver meaningful improvements. Break ambitious initiatives into releases that solve real customer problems. Make clear decisions about scope and sequencing, work through dependencies, and carry the work through to a complete, useful experience.
  • Measure value and follow through. Define success before launch and evaluate what happens afterward through product usage, customer feedback, and measures such as task completion and time to insight. When results fall short, understand why and drive the changes needed to improve them.
  • Champion reporting across the company and with customers. Communicate the vision, demonstrate new capabilities, and help commercial and marketing teams explain their value. Build enthusiasm and adoption while bringing customer feedback into the next round of product decisions.

What You Bring to the Table

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with a track record of taking software products from discovery through launch and continued improvement.
  • Clear communication and independent execution. You write persuasive vision and requirements documents, make complex ideas understandable, and explain decisions and tradeoffs with precision. You build alignment across teams and move work forward through ambiguity and dependencies.
  • Experience building data products people rely on. You have delivered analytics or reporting products involving capabilities such as data exploration, visualization, reporting APIs, scheduled delivery, or data collaboration. You understand what makes these products useful in customers’ daily workflows and what it takes to earn their trust.
  • Hands-on fluency with data. You’re strong in SQL and comfortable exploring datasets, investigating discrepancies, and testing hypotheses yourself. You understand data modeling, metric definitions, and how granularity, freshness, and quality affect an analysis. You bring an analytical mindset and know how to use visualization and data storytelling to make complex information clear and actionable.
  • Technical depth and a collaborative approach to building. You enjoy working closely with engineers on data pipelines, APIs, query performance, and the models that underpin reporting. You can translate customer needs into meaningful technical requirements and reason through tradeoffs across flexibility, latency, reliability, and scale.
  • Strong product judgment and attention to craft. You simplify complex problems, recognize the details that matter, and make scope decisions that preserve the value of the experience.
  • A keen eye for UX and a bias toward simplicity. You know the best experiences feel simple because someone made difficult decisions about what to leave out, and you partner with designers to push for clarity, especially in data-dense products.
  • Customer curiosity backed by action. You spend time with users, use the products you manage, and translate what you learn into clear priorities and useful solutions.
  • A commitment to measurable outcomes. You use evidence to evaluate whether a product is delivering value, recognize when your assumptions were wrong, and follow through on improvements.

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with digital advertising, programmatic platforms, or advertiser and agency workflows.
  • Experience building AI-native analytics or reporting products that rethink how people—and agents—work with data. This could include conversational exploration, automated investigations, proactive insights, or APIs and tools that enable agents to query data, reason over results, and take action. We’re especially interested in builders who have moved beyond demos to useful experiences, with thoughtful approaches to accuracy, evaluation, permissions, and user trust.

title: Sanitation Worker
description:
The Janitor / Sanitation Specialist maintains a clean, safe, and audit-ready Grower/Processor
facility. This role performs daily housekeeping and janitorial tasks; manages laundry for scrubs
and uniforms; executes cannabis-specific sanitation (rooms, tools, equipment) using approved
chemicals; and supports compliant waste handling and disposal. Works across cultivation,
post-harvest/cure, extraction-adjacent areas, packaging, warehouse/vault, offices, restrooms,
and common spaces—following SOPs, safety rules, and documentation standards. This is a full time position that will included benefits.

Responsibilities
General Housekeeping: Janitorial
  1. Clean and restock restrooms and break areas; sweep/mop floors; dust/clean surfaces and high-touch points; remove trash and recyclables.
  2. Maintain entrances, hallways, offices, and common areas to 5S standards; stage supplies (liners, towels, soap, sanitizer).
  3. Production-Area Sanitation (Cannabis-Specific)
  4. Sanitize processing rooms (dry, cure, trim, packaging) and cultivation support spaces per frequency (daily/weekly/deep clean).
  5. Clean equipment exteriors, carts, bins, tables, and drains; follow validated dilutions/contact times and color-coded tools to prevent cross-contamination.
  6. Document all sanitation tasks on approved logs; support line-clearance cleaning between strains/lots as scheduled.
  7. Laundry (Scrubs & Uniforms) Collect, launder, dry, and stage clean garments; manage size assortments and par levels; operate machines safely and maintain filters/chemicals.
  8. Segregate soiled vs. clean; follow contamination-control practices; log loads and chemical usage.
  9. Waste Handling & Disposal. Segregate general waste, recyclables, and cannabis process waste per SOPs; ensure containers are labeled, closed, and staged in designated areas.
  10. Assist with rendering cannabis waste non-consumable (e.g., mixing with non-usable material) under supervision; complete required logs and transfers.
  11. Coordinate pickups with Facilities or licensed vendors; keep staging areas tidy and compliant.
  12. Chemical Management & Safety
  13. Mix and label sanitation chemicals to spec (no off-label use); maintain SDS access and secondary container labels.
  14. Use required PPE; practice safe lifting/ergonomics; place wet-floor signage; report hazards immediately.
  15. Documentation & Communication
  16. Complete sanitation, laundry, and waste logs accurately and on time; support audits with clean, current records.
  17. Communicate low stock, equipment issues (vacuums, washers, autoscrubbers), or room access conflicts to the Manager promptly.

Qualifications:
  1. 1+ year janitorial/housekeeping or sanitation experience in manufacturing, food/CPG, healthcare, or cannabis preferred.
  2. Able to read/follow SOPs, dilution charts, and SDS; basic recordkeeping on paper or tablet.
  3. Reliable, detail-oriented, and safety-minded; excellent attendance and time management.

Physical Rquirements:

Stand/walk for extended periods; lift/push/pull up to 50 lbs; frequent bending/reaching. Work in varied environments: warm/humid grow rooms, cool/dry rooms, wet cleaning areas, and standard office spaces; routine exposure to sanitation chemicals (PPE provided/required).

national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, sexual orientation, genetic information,
pregnancy, sex, gender identity or expression, disability, or because of the liability for service in
the armed forces of the United States or the nationality of any individual, or any other
characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. ​

title: Technical Deputy Program Manager

Lawelawe is a Native Hawaiian Owned Small Disadvantaged Business that provides professional and mission-support services to federal Government customers. As the Technical Deputy Program Manager, serving as the Program Manager’s principal deputy and Lawelawe’s senior representative on the contract. Reporting to and supporting the Program Manager, you will guide technical resources, oversee software development from initial design through release, and coordinate Lawelawe personnel and subcontractor support.   • Translate contractual requirements and agency objectives into technical priorities, requirements, specifications, and executable workflows.
  • Manage software development projects from design through completion, including analysis, design, development of enhancements and new modules, testing, evaluation, and release.
  • Partner with the Program Manager and Product Owners to define product strategy, forecast development needs, and plan and execute the product roadmap.
  • Research product development options and recommend technical approaches and product direction.
  • Facilitate Agile/Scrum ceremonies and technical governance reviews, providing teams with clear direction, resources, and realistic schedule and cost estimates.
  • Coordinate deployment of functional improvements within approved release schedules and promote continuous technical improvement.
  • Partner with the Program Manager to manage scope, schedule, resources, and cost baselines and track performance against contract requirements.
  • Identify program risks, operational bottlenecks, and engineering issues; implement corrective actions and escalate matters requiring additional authority.
  • Work with the Program Director, Program Manager, customer, technical leads, and program staff to meet staffing and performance needs.
  • Coordinate with Government stakeholders, corporate leadership, subcontractors, and program teams to align priorities and resolve technical and operational issues.
  • Prepare program reports, deliverables, executive briefings, and written updates that clearly communicate technical metrics, progress, risks, and decisions needed.

The Team

Our team brings together program management and technical professionals who work collaboratively to support customer priorities. You will partner with program leadership, development teams, corporate support functions, and subcontractors to deliver reliable solutions and maintain consistent program performance.

Here's What You Need

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • At least seven (7) years of experience in software product design, development, release, and delivery, including at least five (5) years of management or leadership experience within a software development organization and at least two (2) years managing a Scrum team.
  • Demonstrated ability to serve as a program’s second in charge and assume daily program leadership during the Program Manager’s absence.
  • Ability to serve as senior contract representative, lead assigned employees, coordinate subcontractor support, and communicate with Government and corporate leadership.
  • Experience with risk management, issue resolution, and problem-solving.
  • Knowledge of system architectures, networks, and operations.
  • United States citizenship and ability to provide proof of citizenship.
  • Ability to successfully complete required background screening and satisfy applicable Government suitability requirements to obtain a Public Trust.

Additional Qualifications

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical information to internal and external stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-resolution skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and provide strategic direction.
  • Ability to anticipate and respond proactively to technical and operational challenges.
  • Experience applying Agile principles and Scrum methodology across development teams.
  • Commitment to continuous learning and professional development.

Bonus Points If You Have

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
  • Agile credentials such as Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP), or SAFe Agilist/Product Manager.
  • Relevant domain certifications such as ITIL, CISSP, or AWS/Azure architect certifications.

Work Location

This is a remote position located in San Antonio, Texas.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation package.
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.
  • Company-sponsored retirement plans with matching contributions.
  • Professional development and continued learning opportunities.
  • Additional perks and discounts available to employees.

Compensation

Salary is dependent on experience (DOE) and will be determined based on qualifications, relevant experience, and applicable requirements.


The above job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Candidates possessing the necessary qualifications for the position will be considered.

Lawelawe Technology Services is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status, and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

Offers of employment are contingent upon satisfactory completion of a comprehensive background verification, inclusive of a criminal record check. Employment may be subject to other background checks, as required by the position.

  • Generous Time Off to Recharge and Maintain Work-Life Balance: Up to 22 days off in your first year, increasing to 26 days after 12 months.
  • Flexible Hybrid Role: We offer remote flexibility, allowing you to balance your clinical work and administrative tasks on your terms. Telehealth is determined by the BCBA when it's clinical effective for the client and BT.
  • CEU Stipend: $2,000 annually to support your continued professional development.
  • License Reimbursement: We cover the cost of your BCBA license renewal.

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: Including medical, dental, vision, life, disability insurance, plus pet insurance—because we care about your entire family, furry friends included!
  • Set Scheduling: Predictable work hours help you balance your work and personal life.

Your Role and Impact:

As a BCBA at Cortica, you’ll play a pivotal role in overseeing neurodiversity-affirming clinical programming for patients receiving ABA treatment. You'll lead a team of behavior technicians (BTs) empowering them to make a lasting difference in the lives of children with developmental differences.


What you’ll love about this role:

  • Achievable Targets: You’ll average 26 billable hours per week, with reduced targets during shorter weeks to ensure a manageable workload.
  • Industry-Leading Dual Bonus Program: Enjoy two separate bonus opportunities that reward your impact and leadership.
    - Productivity Bonus: Increase your earning potential through flexible productivity incentives designed to reward additional billable hours while maintaining work-life balance.
    - ABA Caseload Bonus: Earn additional monthly bonus opportunities based on ABA direct service hours billed and converted within your POD, with bonus potential up to 10% of monthly base salary.
  • Growth and Advancement Opportunities: You'll have the chance to advance through BCBA levels I, II, III, and IV, increasing your leadership impact along the way. At BCBA levels III and IV, productivity targets are reduced to 22, allowing you to focus on developing leadership skills, cultivating other talents, and exploring broader professional interests.
  • Autonomy over Your Schedule: You’ll have full control over when and where you supervise your cases, empowering you to design a schedule that works for you.
  • Administrative Support: Focus on what you do best—clinical care—while our dedicated team handles scheduling, billing, and credentialing, leaving you with more time to focus on your work and patients.

Qualifications and Requirements:

  • Master’s degree in human services or a related field.
  • Current BCBA (Board-Certified Behavior Analyst) Certification required.

What Makes Cortica Different from Other ABA Companies?

At Cortica, we believe in going beyond traditional ABA practices to offer a more comprehensive, patient-centered approach that is different from other ABA companies:

  • A Transdisciplinary Approach to Care: Unlike many ABA companies that focus solely on behavior therapy, Cortica offers a holistic, multidisciplinary model of care. Our team includes experts from a wide range of fields—occupational therapy, speech pathology, pediatrics, and more—allowing us to address the whole child and deliver more integrated, effective care.
  • Focus on Collaboration: At Cortica, we don’t just implement therapy—we collaborate with families, caregivers, and other clinicians to create individualized care plans that empower everyone involved. This approach ensures that each child’s unique needs are met, and that the entire team is aligned in their goals for success.
  • Quality Over Quantity: We take pride in value-based care partnerships with health plans that prioritize quality over quantity. Our patients benefit from the time we dedicate to collaborative, integrated care, and our clinicians are supported with more time for thoughtful clinical decision-making. Unlike other providers, we are reimbursed based on outcomes, not just the number of sessions delivered.

By joining Cortica, you’ll be part of a team that’s redefining ABA therapy—combining compassion, innovation, and collaboration to deliver results that matter.

title: Travel Manager
description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit .

Role Overview:

CHAOS is scaling quickly, and so is our travel. Engineers, program teams, and field personnel are regularly on complex, multi-leg international itineraries, often to regions with elevated security, health, and geopolitical risk. Today that burden falls on individual travelers and their teams. We are hiring a Travel Manager to own the travel function end to end: administering our travel platform (Navan), supporting travelers before and during trips, building the duty-of-care program that keeps people safe in difficult places, and controlling travel spend without slowing the company down.

This role sits in Finance and reports to the Controller, working day to day with Security, IT, People, and the program teams who travel most. You will own the completion of our Navan rollout, the corporate travel policy, our preferred-vendor programs, and the emergency response playbook for travelers in high-risk locations. The right person is equally comfortable rebooking a stranded traveler on short notice and walking leadership through travel spend trends.


Responsibilities:

Travel platform ownership (Navan)

  • Serve as system administrator for Navan: user provisioning, policy configuration, approval workflows, cost-center and department mapping, and integration with our expense and accounting systems.
  • Lead completion of the Navan migration and drive adoption across the company.
  • Maintain preferred vendor programs, negotiated rates, and corporate accounts with airlines, hotels, and ground transportation providers.
  • Own reporting on travel spend, policy compliance, and vendor performance; identify and recommend savings opportunities.

Traveler support and complex itineraries

  • Act as the primary point of contact for travel questions, changes, and disruptions, including after-hours escalation for travelers in transit.
  • Plan and book complex multi-leg international itineraries, including travel to remote or high-risk locations with limited commercial options.
  • Coordinate visas, entry requirements, vaccinations, and country-specific documentation; track passport and visa expirations for frequent travelers.
  • Partner with program and field teams on advance planning for deployments, test events, and customer site visits.

Duty of care and risk

  • Build and maintain our duty-of-care program: traveler tracking, pre-trip risk briefings, check-in protocols, and emergency response procedures.
  • Coordinate with Security, IT, and outside providers (travel security, medical evacuation, insurance) to support employees traveling to hostile or sanctioned regions.
  • Ensure travel processes account for export control and device-handling requirements, working with Security and Compliance on the applicable rules.
  • Monitor advisories and events that may affect travelers and proactively adjust plans.

Policy and process

  • Own the corporate travel policy: draft, update, communicate, and enforce it in a way that works for a fast-moving engineering organization.
  • Design approval and exception workflows that balance traveler flexibility with cost and risk control.
  • Support the Accounting team on travel-related close activities, accruals, and reconciliations with the expense platform.
  • Travel: occasional (less than 10%), primarily to CHAOS offices and vendor meetings.
  • Physical demands: standard office environment; must be reachable for traveler emergencies outside normal business hours on a rotating or as-needed basis.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Minimum education: Bachelor's degree in business, hospitality, international affairs, or another related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • Hands-on experience administering a corporate travel platform (Navan, Concur, Egencia, or similar), including policy configuration and approval workflows.
  • Demonstrated experience booking and supporting complex international itineraries, including travel to high-risk or logistically difficult regions.
  • Working knowledge of duty-of-care practices, traveler risk management, and emergency response coordination.
  • Ability to navigate visa and entry requirements quickly and accurately under time pressure.
  • Experience building travel spend and compliance reporting and explaining it to a non-finance audience.
  • Strong service orientation with the judgment to enforce policy without becoming a bottleneck.
  • Willingness to be reachable for traveler emergencies outside normal business hours.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Experience in defense, aerospace, government contracting, energy, NGO, or another industry with frequent travel to high-risk regions.
  • Navan administration experience specifically, including a platform migration or initial rollout.
  • Experience supporting travel for personnel operating under export control regimes (e.g., ITAR/EAR) or holding security clearances.
  • Experience with Ramp or a similar expense platform and its integration with travel tools.
  • Vendor negotiation experience with airlines, hotel chains, or travel management companies.

Why CHAOS?

  • Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company
  • Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more
  • Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code
  • Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses
  • Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices
Salary Range: $105,000 - $132,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.

title: Case Manager
description:
Title: Case Manager
Division: Project 180
Pay Scale: $25.24 - $30.62


Project 180 Overview

Mission: SSG-Project 180 provides practical and clinical behavioral health, re-entry, and diversion solutions that empower justice-involved Angelenos to achieve lasting personal transformation and reclaim their lives.

Org. Summary: Project 180 is a leader in the forensic treatment space, offering high-quality, specialized treatment programs that serve thousands of justice-involved individuals. Our programs span criminal justice intercepts and include pre-arrest interventions, court-based diversions, jail in-reach, and intensive post-release services. Project 180 operates in partnership with County agencies including the Department of Mental Health (DMH), the Department of Health Services (DHS), and the Justice, Care and Opportunities Department (JCOD). Annually, we serve over 1,500 justice-involved individuals.

At the heart of our organization are our core values - our fundamental, non-negotiable beliefs that guide how we make decisions and work with one another in service of our mission:

Humanity: We lead with a people-centered focus, seeking to understand and value the lived experience of others and centering their human dignity.

Integrity: We honor the trust placed in us by doing what is right while fulfilling our commitments - even when no one is watching.

Adaptability: We embrace the pivot, evolving to meet the complex needs of our community.

Empowerment: We cultivate the tools, confidence, resilience, optimism, and agency within every individual to lead their own transformation.

Equity: We honor everyone’s unique journey, meet them where they are and commit to providing the targeted support and resources that allow each individual to contribute and thrive.

Interdependence: We move as a unified team, trading silos for collective strength, recognizing that our greatest impact is achieved together.


The Program

The Full Service Partnership (FSP) program adopts a “whatever it takes” approach to provide intensive, wraparound, field based services to adults who have significant mental health problems. The FSP program assists with housing, employment and education in addition to providing mental health services and integrated treatment for individuals who have a co-occurring mental health and substance abuse disorder. Services can be provided to individuals in their homes, the community and other locations.

The Position

Under the supervision of the Program Supervisor, the FSP Case Manager is responsible for providing intensive, wraparound, field based case management services. Case Managers also serve as a member of a multidisciplinary treatment team. A successful FSP case manager will actively engage this population in services, supporting their clients in making progress towards meaningful recovery goals and increasing utilization of community resources to help clients find and keep competitive and integrated employment. The FSP Case Manager will be trained and utilize the evidence-based Individual Placement and Support (IPS) model to support clients employment goals. Job title (I-III) to be established based on years of relevant experience.



Essential Functions

Provide intensive, wraparound, field-based services to support recovery goals

  • Actively engage clients in services through the development of strong rapport, consistent contact and use of motivational interviewing. Provide outreach services as needed, meeting clients “where they are at” (service location, client’s point of view).
  • Services to target cornerstones of recovery oriented care (instilling hope, empowerment, self-responsibility and engaging in meaningful roles). Ensure service delivery is consistent with ethical standards and a harm reduction, strength based, trauma informed framework.
  • Develop and maintain knowledge of available community resources. Complete needs assessment and link clients to community resources. Monitor ongoing participation in services/use of resources and facilitate problem solving to target barriers. Accompany clients to linkage appointments when appropriate.
  • Teach prosocial and recovery skills (ie communication, problem solving, anger management skills) for long term stability in the community.
  • Engage and join with collaterals (family members, probation, court) as appropriate. Provide education related to mental health recovery to better support clients. Engage in client advocacy.
  • Conduct custody pick ups from LA county jails
  • Apply evidence-based Individual Placement and Support (IPS) model to help clients find and keep meaningful, competitive employment.
  • Provide direct support for resume tailoring, online job applications, interview preparation, and disclosure decisions.

description:

title: Network Management Specialist
description:
ABOUT ENABLE DENTAL

Enable Dental is redefining dental care by bringing high-quality, comprehensive services directly to those who need it most—patients in assisted living facilities, skilled nursing homes, and individuals unable to visit a traditional office. By combining cutting-edge mobile healthcare technology with a compassionate, skilled team, we’re improving oral health outcomes and enhancing quality of life for thousands of patients.

As a rapidly growing, mission-driven company, we foster a high-performance culture where innovation, accountability, and teamwork drive everything we do. If you're looking for a career with purpose and growth potential, this is your opportunity to make a real impact.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a high-ownership, relationship-driven Network Management Specialist to recruit, onboard, and manage dental specialists as we build and scale our national specialty network. This role is critical to ensuring our patients have access to high-quality specialty care—including oral surgery, endodontics, periodontics, and other disciplines—within our mobile care model.

You will partner directly with the COO to design and execute our specialist network strategy: identifying target markets, recruiting top-tier providers, negotiating agreements, ensuring credentialing readiness, and driving long-term engagement and performance.

This is a high-impact, cross-functional role that blends business development, provider relations, contracting, and operational execution.

YOUR DAY TO DAY

  • Recruit & Build the Network
    • Identify priority markets and specialty gaps based on growth strategy and patient demand
    • Proactively source, recruit, and onboard high-quality dental specialists
    • Conduct outreach campaigns, manage pipeline tracking, and drive signed agreements
  • Own Provider Relationships
    • Serve as the primary relationship manager for contracted specialists
    • Ensure alignment on expectations, scheduling, quality standards, and performance metrics
    • Address issues quickly and professionally to maintain strong engagement
  • Contracting & Negotiation
    • Lead compensation discussions and contract execution in partnership with leadership
    • Ensure agreements align with margin targets and operational realities
  • Credentialing & Readiness
    • Partner with operations and credentialing teams to ensure specialists are fully compliant and launch-ready
    • Maintain accurate provider data and documentation
  • Performance & Optimization
    • Monitor utilization, productivity, case acceptance, and patient access metrics
    • Identify opportunities to improve specialist engagement and clinical throughput
    • Support ongoing optimization of specialty workflows
  • Strategic Growth
    • Provide market intelligence and competitive insights
    • Contribute to long-term specialty expansion planning
    • Support new market launches and enterprise client expansions

WHY YOU’LL LOVE THIS ROLE

  • Direct Impact: Your work directly expands patient access to critical specialty dental care.
  • Executive Visibility: You’ll report to the COO and play a central role in strategic growth decisions.
  • Builder Opportunity: This is not maintenance mode—you’ll help design and scale the network from the ground up.
  • Mission-Driven Work: We serve patients who otherwise face significant barriers to care.
  • High-Growth Environment: Join a company scaling rapidly with meaningful leadership opportunities ahead.

Requirements

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • 3–7+ years of experience in provider recruitment, network development, healthcare contracting, or related roles
  • Experience recruiting or managing healthcare providers (dental experience strongly preferred)
  • Strong relationship-building and negotiation skills
  • Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple markets and provider pipelines simultaneously
  • Analytical mindset with comfort reviewing utilization and performance data
  • Self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, growth-stage environment
  • Exceptional communication skills—professional, clear, and persuasive

Benefits

Perks: Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes Medical, Dental, Vision coverage, a 401(k) plan (with 3% match), Life Insurance, and generous Paid Time Off to help you recharge and thrive

Base salary: $70,000-$80,000 (depending on experience)

The role carries full P&L responsibility — including budget, team leadership, delivery performance, and governance — and is accountable for originating and closing real estate development and investment opportunities, structuring and negotiating deals, and securing complex development and partnership agreements through traditional and non-traditional structures.

Success in this role means converting development opportunities into signed agreements and long-term revenue streams, delivering scalable real estate assets, and building and maintaining relationships with capital partners and government stakeholders. This requires deep real estate development experience within complex enterprises, paired with an entrepreneurial, execution-focused approach — the ability to move decisively from strategy to results while navigating matrixed internal and external stakeholder environments and operating effectively within enterprise financial, governance, compliance, and decision-making structures.

  • Effectively align systems and structures across teams to maximize impact and operational effectiveness.
  • Provide day-to-day leadership to develop and execute plans that maximize development opportunities and manage risk.
  • Ensure program compliance with legal, contractual, and government requirements while enabling speed of execution and risk-informed decisions.
  • Provide timely, accurate reporting on operating performance, risks, and opportunities to enable executive decisions and proactive risk mitigation; coordinate functional support leads to deliver shared enterprise initiatives.
  • Model the highest standards of business professionalism; lead the training and development of team members through coaching, motivating, and mentoring on company culture, business goals, fiscal responsibility, and sound business judgment.
  • Lead the recruitment and retention of a diverse team of development, operations, and finance professionals; create accountability and ownership through clear expectations, supervision, and timely performance feedback.

Role Specific Requirements Include:

  • Bachelor's degree required; MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.
  • 20+ years of progressive real estate development leadership experience with a demonstrated track record of enterprise growth.
  • Proven record of winning and scaling complex real estate transactions, including complex, multi-year, multi-stakeholder development programs.

  • Experience working within large, matrixed organizations while delivering entrepreneurial, execution-focused outcomes.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to anticipate real estate market trends, identify development opportunities, and drive execution.
  • Executive presence and ability to influence senior stakeholders, demonstrating a high political and organizational acumen.
  • Ability to operate effectively in highly regulated environments, ensuring compliance, risk management, and governance while maintaining speed of development and execution.

Exceptional Benefits for Exceptional Team Members

The annual salary range for this position is estimated to go from the mid to upper $300's, depending on experience, skills, qualifications, and work location. This position is eligible for a discretionary target incentive of up to 50% of the base salary.

title: Manager, Youth Services
description:
ANALYTICAL ● DECISIVE ● EMPATHETIC ● RESULTS-DRIVEN ● SUPPORTIVE

Our client is a growing, community-based organization that provides support for youth in the Region of Peel. They are a leading organization recognized for their commitment to providing youth with the resources and services to help them achieve independence and growth. The organization is looking for passionate people to join their vision and mission!

Are you passionate about accounting and supporting vulnerable youth?

The Pod Group is partnering with this amazing organization to place a resourceful, hands-on, and organized individual to fulfill the role of Manager, Youth Services.

WHY YOUR ROLE MATTERS 🔍

Reporting to the Director of Youth Services and Wellness, you will guide the work of a multidisciplinary team including mental health and addictions specialists and intensive case managers. You will manage all clinical services and intensive case management functions at the organization, including crisis response services, individual and group clinical interventions, housing stabilization supports, and youth-centered case management. You will work with the Director to implement and maintain integrated practice standards informed by Assertive Community Treatment, Housing First for Youth, harm reduction, and trauma-informed care principles.

You will drive effective service coordination for youth with complex needs across organizational service areas, including central intake, shelter, housing, prevention services, and community partnerships.

The Manager, Youth Services will lead, elevate, engage and deliver the innovative and highly effective supports based on the following:

  1. Trauma-Informed Principles
  2. Clinical Assessment and Treatment Planning
  3. Relationship-Centered Approach
  4. Strengths-Based & Anti-Oppressive Approach
  5. Housing First and Harm Reduction Philosophy
  6. Multidisciplinary and Coordinated Care
  7. Cultural Sensitivity & Intersectionality
  8. Ongoing Supervision and Reflective Practice
  9. Advocacy and Systems Navigation
  10. Aftercare Support and Evaluation

Working within a trauma-informed, anti-oppressive, and harm reduction framework, the Manager, Youth Services supports a continuum of intervention services that promote housing stability, wellness, mental health recovery, and long-term positive outcomes for youth experiencing homelessness.

HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT 🎯

  • Lead integrated programs and services. Using Assertive Community Treatment, Housing First for Youth, and Harm Reduction principles and best practices, you will develop and manage the delivery of integrated and coordinated supports for youth (ages 16-24) receiving services from the organization. Overseeing a team of mental health and addictions specialists and intensive case managers, you will shape and evolve the team's vision, philosophy, and objectives while managing projects that align internal operations with the evolving landscape of wraparound support for youth experiencing homelessness. Programs in this portfolio include the following:
    • Clinical interventions – You will oversee the delivery of rapid crisis response, mental health and addictions assessments, individual and group counselling, treatment planning, and clinical consultation across all organizational sites.
    • Intensive Case Management – Using the Assertive Community Treatment model, you will oversee the delivery of youth-driven intensive case management services based on Housing First for Youth principles, including assessment, care planning, housing stabilization, systems navigation, advocacy, safety planning, and service coordination.
    • Service Integration and Care Coordination - You will ensure effective integration between clinical services, shelter services, housing supports, prevention services, and community partners to facilitate seamless service delivery and positive youth outcomes.
    • Ongoing Quality Improvement - You will continuously identify and address barriers to service access while monitoring program effectiveness and implementing evidence-informed improvements across both clinical and case management services.
  • Provide team leadership. Within the Assertive Community Treatment model, you will lead youth assignments, team meetings, rounds, and group supervisions, fostering a cohesive multidisciplinary team that delivers high-quality care. You will provide clinical, practice-based, and administrative supervision to assigned teams and staff. You will lead multidisciplinary case consultations and support integrated service planning to ensure coordinated and client-centered care.
  • Develop Internal Competencies & Capacity Building. You will assess, analyze and prioritize a training and capacity building plan to elevate the awareness and understanding of clinical modalities and competencies of all staff across the organization.
  • Manage documentation. You will create annual work plans for yourself and your team, assign programming duties, and manage youth assignments to ensure prompt support based on service targets. You will establish and enhance systems for crisis triage, service planning, and workload distribution across assigned teams.
  • Evaluate performance. You will conduct reviews of clinical practice, case management interventions, housing outcomes, service plans, and documentation standards to ensure high-quality service delivery and accountability. You will manage bi-annual file audits, provide constructive feedback, and evaluate direct reports to identify growth opportunities. You will participate in program evaluation and continuous improvement efforts.
  • Manage incidents. You will address disciplinary procedures and grievances in consultation with the Senior Director of HR and in accordance with the CBA. You will review and approve serious occurrences and critical incident reports, ensuring appropriate follow-up within the clinical team.
  • Provide oversight. You will work with managers and external partners to develop and deliver evidence-based, collaborative programs. You will oversee the acquisition of clinical resources and equipment and ensure the delivery of psychological health and safety practices at the organization. You will maintain strict client confidentiality and participate in the agency's on-call rotation.
  • Ensure risk and compliance management. You will assess and mitigate risks, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and adherence to professional codes of ethics. You will develop and execute risk management strategies for clinical services.
  • Drive strategic planning. You will integrate research, innovation, and best practices into program delivery while collaborating with leadership and front-line teams to implement effective strategies. Through regular environmental scans, you will evaluate community needs, service delivery outcomes, and partnership opportunities, recommending policy and system improvements.
  • Foster Equity, Diversity, and Belonging. You will embed cultural humility and inclusivity in case consultations and program delivery. Staying updated on best practices in equity and diversity, you will work with leadership to infuse these principles into all operations. As a role model, you will cultivate an inclusive organizational culture and develop leaders, integrating equity and belonging into all interactions and practices.
  • Other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU WILL BRING 🎓

  • Education: You possess a Bachelor's Degree in Social Work, Psychology, Child and Youth Care, Health Sciences, or a related field; a Master's Degree is considered an asset. Registration with a relevant professional regulatory body is preferred. Additional education in mental health, addictions, housing and homelessness, or case management is considered an asset.
  • Experience: You have a minimum 3 years of experience working as a supervisor/manager in the social service sector, preferably with individuals with complex mental health, serious mental illness, and substance use. Youth-specific experience is preferred. Familiarity with Housing First for Youth and Assertive Community Treatment Team models is preferred. Experience supervising multidisciplinary teams consisting of clinicians, case managers, and community support staff is strongly preferred. You have an understanding of concepts related to power and privilege, social location, equity, and intersectionality. You have demonstrable experience in implementing equity strategies in programs and services. You have site and team management experience, including exposure to human resource management (union experience is a strong asset), financial management, program management, evaluation design, or systems design.
  • Knowledge: You possess and can demonstrate strong knowledge of Housing First for Youth, Assertive Community Treatment principles, harm reduction practices, crisis intervention, coordinated care planning, housing stabilization, and youth homelessness service systems. You have a comprehensive knowledge of youth developmental stages, social ecology, and family systems. You are acutely aware of the impact of childhood, racial, and intergenerational trauma on youth development. You demonstrate an understanding of issues relating to youth homelessness and the barriers youth face in attaining and maintaining their housing, as well as an understanding of the broader housing sector in Peel.
  • Leadership: You are a clinical leader with excellent communication, presentation, organization and interpersonal skills with a passion for supporting the most vulnerable and marginalized youth in our community. You leverage relevant information and critical analysis to make informed decisions, tackling problems with urgency and energy. You are passionate about mobilizing individuals and teams to drive change and collaborating with partners and stakeholders at all levels to build consensus.
  • Ethics and Drive: You hold yourself to high moral standards, have a strong character and exercise sound judgment even in the most challenging situations. You are a champion of Equity, Inclusion and Belonging, specifically focusing on Anti-Black Racism. You are thoughtful in your choices and reflective in your guidance and practice, fostering learning, promoting innovation and introducing change for the better. You accept responsibility for decisions and actions and achieve results utilizing accountability strategies with staff.
  • You have flexibility to work in a 24-hour, 7 days a week operation, while supporting an on-call rotation.
  • You possess a valid Ontario’s full G Driver’s License is required, with a clean driver’s abstract.
  • A $2,000,000 minimum liability car insurance coverage is also mandatory.
  • Must be able to travel and support youth in the community and all locations (local travel is required on a regular basis).
  • You have valid CPI and/or UMAB and First Aid/ CPR certifications.
  • You complete a successful Vulnerable Sector Check/Criminal Record Check as a condition of employment.

OUR COMMITMENT TO EDIB

The success of an organization stems from a team that is aligned with its mission and vision, where decisions are made in the best interests of the clients they serve and the marginalized and vulnerable populations across our communities. Through this effort, all team members embrace their roles in the organization with respect and dignity for all stakeholders. Through these partnerships, everyone is focused on ensuring a commitment and responsibility toward anti-racism, anti-oppression, equity, diversity, inclusivity, and belonging.

OUR PARTNERSHIP - THE POD GROUP

The Pod Group (PG) connects candidates with amazing career opportunities in Ontario! We collaborate extensively with not-for-profit and community-based organizations, including health, social services, developmental, housing, mental health, and community health care.

We promote a unique candidate experience that integrates equity, diversity, inclusion and belonging in our engagement with candidates. Our recruitment strategy focuses on learning more about your career goals and aligning your passion with mission-driven work.

We thank you for your interest in applying!

title: Lead AI Engineer
description:
Role Overview

Our product is only as good as the AI behind it. As Lead AI Engineer, you will own the technical direction and quality of Axya's AI systems: how they reason over messy enterprise data, how we measure whether they are right, and how we ship improvements safely to production.

You will report to the CTO and work closely with Product, Customer Success and the engineers who build our platform and integrations. You will be hands-on in the code, and you will also raise the technical bar for the team through architecture, evaluation, code review and mentorship. As the team grows, your scope can grow with it.


What You'll Own

  • The architecture of Axya's AI layer: agent and LLM workflows, retrieval, tool use, and how they connect to customer ERP and procurement data.
  • Evaluation and quality: build the eval frameworks, test sets and monitoring that tell us whether the copilot is accurate, reliable and improving. Be the person who can say "this is ready" and prove it.
  • Production delivery: take AI features from prototype to dependable, observable, cost-aware production systems.
  • Model and tooling decisions: choose, benchmark and evolve models, vendors and frameworks, balancing quality, latency, cost and customer data constraints.
  • Customer-grade reliability and security: work with the CTO and security lead to meet enterprise expectations on data handling, access control, privacy and auditability.
  • Technical standards and mentorship: set engineering practices for AI development and coach other engineers in applied AI.
  • Closing the loop with customers: turn real customer usage and failure cases into the next round of improvements.


What We’re Looking For

Must Have

  • Experience shipping LLM-based or ML-powered systems to production, with real users and real consequences, not only prototypes.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: fluency in Python and comfort building and operating backend services.
  • Hands-on experience with the core building blocks of applied AI: prompting and tool use, retrieval, agent and workflow orchestration, and evaluation.
  • Sound technical judgment: you can make architecture tradeoffs, explain them clearly and own the outcome.
  • Technical leadership: setting direction, reviewing others' work, mentoring or leading projects, even without formal reports.
  • Clear communication with both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience with enterprise or B2B products where reliability, security and customer trust are non-negotiable.
  • Experience with messy structured data from ERP, supply chain, procurement, finance or operations systems.
  • Experience building evaluation and observability tooling for non-deterministic systems.
  • Experience in an early-stage or high-growth environment, or evidence of building something from a blank page.
  • Experience managing cost, latency and model-selection tradeoffs at scale.

Nice to Have

  • Fine-tuning or model adaptation experience.
  • Experience in manufacturing, procurement or supply-chain domains.
  • Familiarity with enterprise security and compliance expectations (SOC 2, data residency, etc.).
  • Fluency in French.

We do not require a specific number of years, a degree, or a particular employer background. We care about what you have built and what it achieved.

AI & Technology Expectations

You will use AI to build AI. We expect you to use coding assistants, automated evaluation, synthetic test generation and agentic workflows to move faster and raise quality, while applying your own judgment on what to trust. We care about how you multiply your own output and the team's, not which specific tools you favor. We also expect you to keep a clear view of the risks: hallucination, data leakage, drift and cost.


What Success Looks Like

After 30 days

  • You understand the current architecture, the main customer use cases and where the AI fails today.
  • You have shipped at least one meaningful improvement or fix.
  • You have a written assessment of the biggest technical risks and opportunities.

After 90 days

  • A baseline evaluation framework is in place and used in release decisions.
  • You have led delivery of one major AI feature or re-architecture to production.
  • Quality, latency and cost are measured and visible to the team.

After 6 to 12 months

  • Accuracy and reliability on core customer workflows have improved by a measurable margin.
  • An AI engineering roadmap is co-owned with Product and the CTO.
  • Repeatable practices (evals, release process, observability) are followed by other engineers.
  • If hiring begins, you have shaped the profile and bar for the next AI and ML hires.


Why Join Axya

  • 🏖 Unlimited vacation policy: because we believe in balance.
  • 🏥 Comprehensive health insurance: your well-being matters.
  • 🕒 Flexible work schedule: results matter more than hours.
  • 🏡 100% remote: get the job done wherever you prefer.
  • 🚀 Be part of a high-impact, collaborative team making real change in a traditional industry.

title: Cultivation Technician
description:
At Calypso Enterprises, we are working to create the next generation of marijuana products by continuously improving standards of operation, empowering employees, and embracing the community we serve. Through compassion, innovation and excellence, Calypso Enterprises is dedicated to providing the highest quality medical marijuana products to those in the Commonwealth who suffer from chronic conditions.

Role Summary
The Cultivation Technician (Flower) executes hands-on work inside flowering rooms from flip
through harvest. The role follows SOPs for canopy work (trellising, defoliation, pruning),
irrigation/fertigation tasks, environmental monitoring, IPM scouting, data collection, and harvest
readiness support.

This technician helps ensure high-quality, compliant flower is delivered to Post-Harvest on schedule while meeting Calypso’s safety, biosecurity, and quality standards.

Responsibilities
  • Canopy Management
  • Install trellis/netting; tuck, prune, and defoliate per run cards and timing windows.
  • Maintain plant spacing and light distribution; remove senescent material to reduce risk.
  • Support crop steering objectives by executing tasks that drive desired plant architecture.
  • Perform irrigation events as directed; check drippers, lines, timers, and emitters for function.
  • Take and log EC/pH of stock solutions, media runoff, and environmental/irrigation readings.
  • Mix stock solutions under supervision, label containers, and maintain line sanitation SOPs.
  • Environmental Monitoring
  • Record room setpoints and actuals (temp, RH/VPD, CO₂) and verify sensor/monitor placement.
  • Check airflow (fans/filters) and dehumidifiers; report alarms, leaks, or abnormal trends immediately.
  • Complete scouting routes (sticky cards, leaf inspections with loupe), record findings, and flag issues.
  • Follow entry/exit, footwear, and tool protocols; maintain quarantine practices when required.
  • Assist with biological releases or corrective actions under manager/QA direction.
  • Participate in pre-harvest checks (trichome maturity visuals, room clean readiness).
  • Stage carts, sanitize tools, and help coordinate cut-down to meet dry-room reservations and SOP specs.
  • Accurately tag and move plants/parts; capture wet weights and reconcile counts.
  • Clean and disinfect rooms, trellis posts, tools, carts, drains, and floors per frequencies.
  • Restock consumables (gloves, labels, zip ties, shears) and maintain tidy, audit-ready rooms.
  • Complete room logs, IPM logs, sanitation checklists, irrigation records, and calibration sheets accurately.
  • Use labels/scanners/tablets for plant/lot movements; escalate discrepancies the same shift.
  • Support internal/external audits with neat, current records.
Qualifications
  • 1+ year hands-on horticulture/CEA or cannabis cultivation preferred; entry-level candidates with strong plant aptitude considered.
  • Working familiarity with flowering room tasks (trellising, defoliation, irrigation checks, basic steering concepts).
  • Basic understanding of EC/pH, VPD, airflow/dehumidification, and sanitation in controlled environments.
  • Comfortable using tablets/scanners, following digital/printed run cards, and entering data accurately.
  • Detail-oriented, reliable, team-focused; able to maintain pace without sacrificing quality.
Physical & Schedule Requirements
  • Stand/walk for extended periods; frequent bending, reaching, ladder/trellis work at height.
  • Repetitive hand work (tucking/defoliation/pruning); lift/push/pull up to 50 lbs.
  • Work in warm/humid rooms with horticultural lighting and dehumidification systems.
  • Regular exposure to sanitation chemicals per SDS (PPE provided/required).
  • Flexible schedule aligned to crop and harvest cycles, including occasional weekends/holidays.

Diversity and Inclusion

national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, sexual orientation, genetic information,
pregnancy, sex, gender identity or expression, disability, or because of the liability for service in

title: Copy of Systems Engineer I
description:
Position Summary

As a Systems Engineer I, you will play a key role in delivering high-quality technical support to our clients and ensuring their IT systems operate efficiently and effectively. This role requires a strong customer service mindset, technical aptitude, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.


Key Responsibilities (Essential Functions)

  • Provide technical support to clients via phone, email, remote support tools, and onsite visits.
  • Diagnose and resolve hardware, software, Microsoft 365, and network-related issues in a timely and efficient manner.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service while supporting clients both remotely and onsite.

  • Demonstrate initiative, sound judgment, and adherence to established procedures when addressing client issues.
  • Escalate complex technical issues to senior engineers or specialized teams when appropriate.
  • Install, configure, maintain, and support hardware and software systems.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of technical support interactions, troubleshooting steps, and issue resolutions.
  • Stay current on industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices.
  • Travel to client sites and StoredTech office locations as needed (estimated up to 50%).
  • Perform additional duties as assigned by management to support organizational goals and client success.


Required Qualifications

  • 1-3 years of experience in a technical support, help desk, or IT support role.
  • Experience troubleshooting Microsoft 365 environments.
  • Strong knowledge of Windows operating systems.
  • Experience troubleshooting hardware, software, and network-related issues.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
  • Ability to travel to client locations as required.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong foundation in IT concepts, hardware, software, networking, and troubleshooting methodologies.
  • Proven ability to analyze technical issues, identify root causes, and implement effective solutions.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with a customer-first approach.
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
  • Strong organizational and documentation skills.
  • Commitment to delivering a high level of customer satisfaction and service excellence.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a Managed Service Provider (MSP) environment.
  • Familiarity with virtualization technologies, including VMware and Hyper-V.
  • Exposure to cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure and AWS.
  • Technical certifications such as CompTIA A+, Network+, Security+, Microsoft Fundamentals, or similar certifications are a plus.


Work Environment & Physical Requirements

  • Regularly communicate with clients and team members via phone, video conferencing, email, and in person.
  • Perform computer-based work for extended periods and sit and/or stand for up to eight hours per day.
  • Move throughout office and client environments to install, maintain, and troubleshoot equipment.
  • Lift, carry, or assist in moving equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.

Work Schedule

Location Requirement

This is an in-office, client-facing position based in Queensbury, NY. Candidates must reside within a reasonable commuting distance (approximately 60 minutes) of the office at the time of hire or be willing to relocate prior to their start date. Relocation assistance is not provided. Regular travel to client sites is an essential function of this role.

title: Senior IT Systems Engineer
description:
About Care Access

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care. We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow.

With programs like Future of Medicine, which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and Difference Makers, which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Together, we are building a future of health that is better and more accessible for all.

To learn more about Care Access, visit .

How This Role Makes a Difference

The Senior IT Systems Engineer will lead the design, implementation, and continuous optimization of our core enterprise infrastructure, cloud services, and endpoint management systems. In this role, you will champion operational excellence by driving automation, proactively hardening system security, and leading the technical response and root-cause analysis for critical service incidents. Additionally, you will foster a culture of continuous learning by mentoring junior administrators, maintaining high-quality technical documentation, and collaborating cross-functionally on strategic business initiatives and platform migrations.

How You'll Make An Impact

  • Design & implement core infrastructure and systems: Research, design, deploy, and improve enterprise systems (identity, M365, endpoint management, cloud services). Lead upgrades, migrations, and new platform rollouts with clear standards and documentation.
  • Reliability, monitoring, and incident escalation: Own operational excellence for critical services—monitoring/alerting, incident response, root-cause analysis, and permanent fixes. Improve uptime, performance, and security posture through automation and hardening.
  • Security, compliance, and vendor/partner collaboration: Partner with Security and Compliance to implement controls (least privilege, patching, logging, access reviews). Manage vendor escalations, evaluate tools, and ensure systems meet internal standards and audit requirements.
  • Mentor junior system admins and build a robust knowledge base for new hires to the IT team and self-service guides for end users
  • Other Responsibilities:
    • Maintain and continuously improve technical documentation (runbooks, SOPs, architecture diagrams, CMDB/service catalog entries).
    • Participate in on-call rotation and provide escalation support; contribute to incident postmortems and track corrective actions to completion.
    • Contribute to tool evaluations and proof-of-concepts; recommend standards and drive adoption (MDM, EDR, IAM, backup, monitoring).
    • Help implement and test business continuity/disaster recovery runbooks (backup verification, restore tests, DR exercises).
    • Participate in cross-functional projects (e.g., M&A integrations, system migrations, data center/cloud transitions).

The Expertise Required

  • Strong knowledge of enterprise infrastructure: identity/IAM, M365, endpoint management, networking fundamentals, and directory services.
  • Working knowledge of cloud platforms (Azure and/or AWS): core services, IAM, networking, logging, and cost/guardrail concepts.
  • Understanding of security best practices: MFA/conditional access, least privilege, hardening, patch/vulnerability management, and audit logging.
  • Familiarity with IT service management concepts: incident/problem/change management, SLAs, and operational metrics.
  • Knowledge of automation patterns and configuration management concepts (IaC mindset, repeatability, drift prevention).
  • Ability to design and implement scalable, secure systems end-to-end (requirements → architecture → rollout → runbooks).
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across endpoints, identity/auth, networking, and SaaS/cloud dependencies (root-cause oriented).
  • Proficiency in scripting/automation (PowerShell strongly preferred; Python/Bash a plus) for provisioning, reporting, and remediation.
  • Experience with monitoring and observability (log collection, alert tuning, dashboards) and on-call/incident leadership.
  • Solid documentation skills: standards, runbooks, diagrams, and change plans that others can execute.

Certifications/Licenses, Education, and Experience

  • Minimum Education:
    • Bachelor’s Degree or Equivalent
  • Minimum Experience:
    • 7+ years of experience within an information technology specific role

How We Work Together

  • Location: Remote within the United States. This role requires 100% of work to be performed in a remote office environment.
  • Travel: This is a remote position with less than 10% travel requirements. Occasional planned travel may be required as part of the role.

The expected pay range for this role is $120,000 - $170,000 USD per year for full time team members.

This hands-on role ensures garments are accurately tracked, quality-checked, and moved efficiently between clients, clothiers, the showroom, and tailoring teams.   • Coordinate completed garment check-ins from alteration partner; including pickups, and deliveries, ensuring clear communication and timely handoffs between teams.

Additional Support (As Needed)

  • Maintain an organized, polished, and client-ready showroom.
  • Assist with client check-ins, garment pickups, payments, and incoming calls.
  • Support general operational needs, including supplies, facility coordination, and vendor communication.

Qualifications

  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities.
  • Strong communication skills and comfortable working across teams.
  • Dependable, proactive, and comfortable in a fast-paced, client-facing environment.
  • Comfortable using technology and CRM systems.

What Success Looks Like

title: Software Engineer III
description:
