title: Director, Cloud Infrastructure
location: Remote (US East Coast / Eastern Time Zone Preferred)
description:
Convene Hospitality Group (CHG) operates a global portfolio of lifestyle brands focused on creating places and experiences that bring people together. The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well. If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team.

Director, Cloud Infrastructure

We're hiring a Director of Cloud Infrastructure to join Convene Hospitality Group's (CHG) Technology organization. It's a hands-on role with an AI-native mindset. There are no direct reports today. You’ll lead through the platform, redesigning how we deploy and setting the standards our product and corporate engineering teams build on. You'll also run the cloud, AI, and venue infrastructure under our portfolio of brands, from client-facing experiences to the systems that keep our nearly 40 venues running. This is a rebuild. You design it and you build it.

Today, deployments are manual and happen about once a sprint. That's the starting line. You'll rethink how we ship so that deployments are unlocked, safe, secure, and governed.

You'll have high autonomy and real decision-making power over the tools we use and how we build. We're committed to AWS and will build deeply on it. Most of what sits on top is fair game: CI tooling, pipeline design, orchestration patterns, and source control. A decision like Bitbucket versus GitHub is a live call, and it's yours to make. Legacy migration follows the decisions. You make the call, then you do the move. This role will have a lot of influence.

This is a wide seat. You’ll work across product and corporate engineering, and you’re a big part of how we get to AI-first, spec-driven development.

What You’ll Do:

  • Rebuild the deployment path. Own CI/CD end to end: build, release, and rollback. Take us from manual deploys to an automated path.
  • Make it safe, secure and governed. Access control, audit trails, secrets management, environment separation, and a rollback path any engineer can execute.
  • Make the platform calls. Source control, CI tooling, orchestration, and infrastructure-as-code patterns. Jenkins is what we run today; what we run next is up to you. Decide, document the trade-off, then go forth and migrate.
  • Run the AI gateway. Build and operate the layer between our engineers, agents and the models they call: provider routing, key management, rate limits, token metering, and usage logging. Every AI call should be visible, governed, and attributable.
  • Enable AI-first, spec-driven development. Build the environments, pipelines and guardrails that let engineers and agents ship with confidence: ephemeral environments, fast feedback, and automated verification.
  • Model and manage cloud and AI cost. Forecast what AI systems will cost before we commit and give Finance numbers they can plan against. Keep a standing view of where cloud spend goes and why, and partner with teams to help keep it in check.
  • Support in-venue networking applications. Each venue relies on network infrastructure for access control, connectivity, and on-site A/V and production. You’ll give our networking team the visibility to monitor and support the applications that keep those venues running.
  • Build the observability layer. Logging, metrics, alerting, and routing on our Loki/Grafana stack, so every failure reaches a named owner.
  • Spread what you know and what you do. Coordinate with the product engineers and ensure a level of backup: documented runbooks, a named second operator on every critical path, and dissemination of knowledge and function across product and corporate engineering. Within six months, you can take two weeks off and we can trudge through an emergency without interrupting you.

What We Look For:

  • You have 9+ years of experience building and running production cloud infrastructure.
  • You're deep on AWS: multi-account structure, networking, IAM, and container orchestration on EKS and/or ECS. You've operated production workloads through incidents, upgrades, and growth.
  • You're fluent in infrastructure as code (Terraform or equivalent) and treat infrastructure changes with the same rigor as application code: reviewed, versioned, reproducible.
  • You've built or rebuilt a CI/CD pipeline that teams actually use. You know what it takes to move an organization from manual deploys to automated ones, including the trust and process work that comes with it.
  • You think about security and governance as design inputs rather than a review gate. Secrets, least privilege, audit trails, environment isolation, and who is allowed to push what, where.
  • You’ve run AI systems in production, from the gateway layer (access control, provider routing, cost attribution, observability) to LLM-backed features, including their evaluation, monitoring, and versioning. Experience with MLOps is a plus as our needs grow.
  • You can estimate cost and defend the number. You've modeled the spend of an architecture before it was built and adjusted the design when it didn't hold up.
  • You're high agency. You set direction without waiting for a spec, make platform decisions with real consequences, and then own the migration. You hold positions firmly, change them on evidence, and leave behind a written trail.
  • You’re a problem solver. Application and data teams seek you out for collaboration on architecture, debugging, and trade-off analysis.
  • You work in the open and hand things off deliberately. You write the runbook, train the second operator, and measure your success partly by how little depends on you being reachable.
  • You explain decisions, risks and trade-offs clearly to engineers, non-engineers, and executives. You make teammates better through code review, pairing, and mentoring.
  • You use AI agents for real multi-step work beyond autocomplete, and you verify what they produce against the real system.

Compensation:

The above job definition information has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. title: Senior Solutions Architect (Pre-Sales)
description:
Role Overview:

The Senior Solutions Engineer will own the technical side of how Teifi wins work. When a manufacturer with 200,000 SKUs, a 15-year-old ERP and 80 stores asks whether Shopify can run their business, you're the one who finds out, decides how it gets built, and works with the broader team to craft the right solution, estimate the project effort, and finalize the Scope of Work.


This is a pre-sales seat, end to end: first discovery call to a signed statement of work. You will be the reason the work reaching our delivery team is scoped right, priced honestly and buildable as written.


You'll join a growing architecture team of Principal, Solutions and Systems Architects, working alongside our Account Executives and reporting to the Director of Solutions Architecture.



Key Responsibilities:


  • Discovery. Run the technical side of discovery with the clientsIT, e-commerce, finance and store operations leads. Get past the symptom the client describes to the cause underneath it: an integration that never mapped a field, a process that moved into someone's spreadsheet years ago, a workaround nobody has written down. To distill this into a clear set of requirements for solutioning.
  • Solution design. Decide what Shopify does natively, what an existing app or one of our products (like WorkMate) covers, and what genuinely needs custom work.
  • Demos and solution reviews. Present Teifi solutions to clients and handle live technical questions, objections, and share best-in-class recommendations with prospective merchants. Build demo stores and prototypes when a slide won't make the point.
  • Scope and estimate integrity. Author the scope behind the SOW and stand behind the effort in it. Clearly documenting assumptions, When something is out of scope, say so during the deal, not after it. Sometimes the right answer is "not this way", and you'll be trusted to say it.
  • Making it reusable. Turn what you scope into patterns the next deal can start from. We work AI-first, and you'll help shape the tooling and pipelines our team uses to scope and price faster without losing accuracy.


Qualifications:


  • From the agency side: you've been the accountable pre-sales or delivery architect on complex commerce programs (ERP, OMS or POS integrations, replatforms) and can show us scopes that survived delivery.
  • From the brand side: you've run a Shopify commerce platform , lived through a migration experience, , and know the difference between what demos well and what a store associate will do on a busy Saturday. If you've moved between those two worlds, even better.


Must-haves


Unified Commerce Strategy


  • Fluent with platform capabilities: what's native, what should run via first party apps, what requires and should be developed custom.
  • Deep Shopify platform and ecoysytem knowledge is ideal; extensive knowledge of a comparable commerce platform and a fast ramp also works.
  • Owned the solution on complex commerce deals or operations as the person accountable for enterprise commerce replatforming projects.
  • Designs to reduce technical debt; identify the cost of shortcuts and trade-offs.
  • Plan for total cost of ownership: licences, apps, integrations, hosting, run team
  • Understands agentic commerce and its impact and opportunities.
  • Stays up-to-date with the latest emerging technologies and advancements in the unified commerce and broader technology sector.
  • Know the enterprise commerce ISV landscape and integrated systems (OMS, IMS, CDP, EMM, IDP, ERP, CMS, CRM, POS, WMS etc..) with the ability to to identify which, when, where each should or should not be used.


Technical and Agentic depth

  • Builds with agentic AI tools, MCP servers and CLIs
  • Works fluently with GraphQL and REST APIs
  • Crafts solutions with consideration for both backend and frontend fundamentals
  • Understands purpose-built microservices vs iPaas, and able to discern between them.


Commercial Exposure


  • Serves as the technical authority in client-facing calls, handling objections, rejections and making justifications to executive stakeholders.
  • Shape deal structure and phasing with AEs to protect margin
  • Flag technical and delivery risk early; recommends logical scoping and phasing of work.
  • You can turn a business requirement into a scoped, estimated, buildable solution, using Teifi’s pricing methodology, and you know the difference between possible and in scope.


Nice to have

  • Retail and store operations: POS, WMS and OMS experience.
  • Back-end or SaaS platform depth beyond storefront and theme/app work.
  • Hands-on time with the ERPs enterprise brands run: Dynamics F&O, SAP, Epicor, Business Central, NetSuite.
  • Comfort building quick headed or headless prototypes accelerated with the right AI tooling.


Benefits & Perks

  • Ongoing professional development through training programs, certifications, and peer mentorship
  • Hybrid work model depending on role, with a Granville Island office and free on-site parking
  • Flexibility in work hours designed to accommodate appointments and personal responsibilities
  • Comprehensive health and dental coverage in Canada, plus a health spending account
  • Paid office closure between Christmas and New Year’s
  • Regular team culture events, stocked office snacks, and a dog friendly workplace
  • Performance based bonus opportunities for full-time employees
